title: Title: Vertex AI Gemini streaming silently drops per-request timeout, falling back to litellm.request_timeout (6000s)

judge.reasoning: Both patches make the same core change: add a `timeout` parameter to `make_call` and `make_sync_call`, forward it to `client.post(..., timeout=timeout)`, and pass `timeout=timeout` through both streaming `partial(...)` constructions in `VertexLLM`. The independent tests confirm both resolve all five issue scenarios (user client, no client, stall bound, error message, httpx.Timeout object). Differences: (1) Patch B also bakes the timeout into the fallback `HTTPHandler(timeout=timeout)` exactly as the issue's suggested fix does, so a freshly created client is correct even without the per-call override; Patch A relies solely on the post-level argument. (2) Tests: Patch B adds focused unit tests in the existing gemini test module that assert the actual httpx request `timeout` extension equals the 2s timeout for sync-no-client, sync-with-user-client, and async paths, using respx/MockTransport consistent with the surrounding file; these would fail before and pass after. Patch A's tests are integration tests depending on `integration._support.wire` and `integration._support.vertex` helpers that are not part of the diff and whose existence cannot be verified, and they expect `MidStreamFallbackError` for a mid-stream stall rather than directly verifying the propagated timeout value. That makes A's test evidence weaker and more fragile. (3) Scope: Patch B additionally forwards `timeout` in the agent_engine streaming wrappers with tests; this is adjacent work beyond the ask but small, tested, and low risk, so it is neutral. Overall B is the more complete fix with more reliable, targeted tests.

issue_md:
Summary
When calling litellm.completion(..., stream=True) against a Vertex AI / Google AI Studio Gemini model, the per-request timeout argument is silently discarded. Streams that stall before the first token hang for the full litellm.request_timeout (default 6000s = 100 minutes) instead of failing at the configured timeout. The non-streaming branch of the same handler propagates timeout correctly — only the streaming branch is broken.

Version
litellm == 1.83.0 (also reproduces on main as of filing)
Python 3.10
Provider: vertex_ai and gemini (both routes through the same handler)
Repro
import litellm
import time

# Set a small request_timeout so the bug doesn't take 100 minutes to surface.
# In practice, the bug means the per-call `timeout` is ignored regardless.
litellm.request_timeout = 30

start = time.monotonic()
try:
    response = litellm.completion(
        model="vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-flash",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}],
        stream=True,
        timeout=2,                  # expect to fail in ~2s on a stalled stream
    )
    for chunk in response:
        pass
except Exception as e:
    print(f"failed after {time.monotonic() - start:.1f}s with: {e!s}")
When the upstream stream stalls (we observe this regularly under load against vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-flash), the call hangs ~30s (the litellm.request_timeout), not ~2s (the per-call timeout). The exception text is also misleading:

litellm.Timeout: Connection timed out after None seconds.
— note the literal None, despite a numeric timeout=2 having been passed.

Root cause
In litellm/llms/vertex_ai/gemini/vertex_and_google_ai_studio_gemini.py, VertexLLM.completion() has two branches. The non-streaming branch correctly bakes the request timeout into the httpx client:

# non-streaming branch (~line 2971)
if client is None or isinstance(client, AsyncHTTPHandler):
    _params = {}
    if timeout is not None:
        if isinstance(timeout, float) or isinstance(timeout, int):
            timeout = httpx.Timeout(timeout)
        _params["timeout"] = timeout
    client = _get_httpx_client(params=_params)
The streaming branch (~line 2944) constructs the make_sync_call partial without any timeout argument:

## SYNC STREAMING CALL ##
if stream is True:
    request_data_str = json.dumps(data)
    streaming_response = CustomStreamWrapper(
        completion_stream=None,
        make_call=partial(
            make_sync_call,
            gemini_client=(
                client
                if client is not None and isinstance(client, HTTPHandler)
                else None
            ),
            api_base=url,
            data=request_data_str,
            model=model,
            messages=messages,
            logging_obj=logging_obj,
            headers=headers,
        ),
        ...
    )
    return streaming_response
make_sync_call itself does not accept a timeout parameter, and its client.post(...) invocation does not pass one:

def make_sync_call(
    client, gemini_client, api_base, headers, data, model, messages, logging_obj,
):
    if gemini_client is not None:
        client = gemini_client
    if client is None:
        client = HTTPHandler()  # uses _DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = httpx.Timeout(5.0, connect=5.0)
    response = client.post(
        api_base, headers=headers, data=data, stream=True, logging_obj=logging_obj,
    )
Net result: the user-supplied timeout is dropped on the floor. Whatever httpx.Client instance is reused/created by make_sync_call is what governs the streaming read timeout.

Why "Connection timed out after None seconds"
In litellm/llms/custom_httpx/http_handler.py:1031, the sync HTTPHandler.post() reports timeouts using its local timeout parameter:

except httpx.TimeoutException:
    raise litellm.Timeout(
        message=f"Connection timed out after {timeout} seconds.",
        model="default-model-name",
        llm_provider="litellm-httpx-handler",
    )
Because make_sync_call calls client.post(...) without a timeout argument, the local timeout is None here even though the actual httpx.Client instance has a real timeout configured. The exception message thus reports None. (The async sibling at line 488 was patched to log Timeout passed={timeout}, time taken={time_delta} — the sync handler was missed.)

Expected behavior
The streaming branch should mirror the non-streaming branch: when timeout is provided to completion(), propagate it down to make_sync_call so that client.post(..., timeout=timeout) enforces the user's configured timeout.

Suggested fix
Two small changes:

Make make_sync_call accept and forward timeout:
def make_sync_call(
    client,
    gemini_client,
    api_base,
    headers,
    data,
    model,
    messages,
    logging_obj,
    timeout: Optional[Union[float, httpx.Timeout]] = None,   # NEW
):
    if gemini_client is not None:
        client = gemini_client
    if client is None:
        client = HTTPHandler(timeout=timeout)                # NEW: bake into fresh client

    response = client.post(
        api_base,
        headers=headers,
        data=data,
        stream=True,
        timeout=timeout,                                     # NEW
        logging_obj=logging_obj,
    )
    ...
Pass timeout through the streaming partial(...) in VertexLLM.completion():
make_call=partial(
    make_sync_call,
    gemini_client=(
        client
        if client is not None and isinstance(client, HTTPHandler)
        else None
    ),
    api_base=url,
    data=request_data_str,
    model=model,
    messages=messages,
    logging_obj=logging_obj,
    headers=headers,
    timeout=timeout,                                         # NEW
),
The async streaming sibling (async_streaming at ~line 2575) already receives timeout via its signature; only the sync streaming path is broken.

Impact
For any sync streaming Gemini call where the upstream stalls before the first chunk:

The user's timeout is ignored.
The call hangs for the full litellm.request_timeout (default 6000s).
The error message reports Connection timed out after None seconds, hiding the actual configured timeout.
In production we observed individual calls hanging 6,008–6,017 seconds — exact matches for litellm.request_timeout=6000 plus connect overhead.

Workaround
Until this is fixed, users of streaming Gemini must rely on application-level timeout managers (e.g., a thread that raises TimeoutError into the main thread) or explicitly construct a short-timeout HTTPHandler and pass it as the client kwarg.

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+import json
+import threading
+import time
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from concurrent.futures import Future, ThreadPoolExecutor
+from concurrent.futures import TimeoutError as FutureTimeout
+from typing import Final
+
+import pytest
+from integration._support.vertex import service_account_json
+from integration._support.wire import Reply, Request, Wire, wire_server
+
+import litellm
+from litellm.exceptions import MidStreamFallbackError
+
+_MODEL: Final = "gemini-3.8-flash"
+_PROJECT: Final = "scripted-project"
+_LOCATION: Final = "us-east5"
+_MESSAGES: Final = [{"role": "user", "content": "does the per-request timeout reach a stalled stream?"}]
+_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: Final = 1.0
+_HANG_DEADLINE_SECONDS: Final = 15.0
+_TOKEN_REPLY: Final = Reply(
+    body=json.dumps({"access_token": "scripted-token", "token_type": "Bearer", "expires_in": 3600}).encode()
+)
+
+
+def _sse(text: str, finish_reason: str | None) -> bytes:
+    candidate: Final = {
+        "content": {"role": "model", "parts": [{"text": text}]},
+        **({"finishReason": finish_reason} if finish_reason else {}),
+    }
+    usage: Final = {"promptTokenCount": 9, "candidatesTokenCount": 2, "totalTokenCount": 11}
+    return b"data: " + json.dumps({"candidates": [candidate], "usageMetadata": usage}).encode() + b"\n\n"
+
+
+def _stream_that_stalls_after_the_first_chunk() -> Reply:
+    return Reply(
+        content_type="text/event-stream",
+        chunks=(_sse("partial", None), _sse("", "STOP")),
+        gate_after_first=threading.Event(),
+    )
+
+
+def _stream_that_completes() -> Reply:
+    return Reply(content_type="text/event-stream", chunks=(_sse("scripted ", None), _sse("answer", "STOP")))
+
+
+def _body_that_stalls_half_way() -> Reply:
+    return Reply(chunks=(b'{"candidates": [', b"]}"), gate_after_first=threading.Event())
+
+
+def _peer(reply: Reply) -> Callable[[Request], Reply]:
+    def respond(request: Request) -> Reply:
+        if request.target == "/_oauth/token":
+            return _TOKEN_REPLY
+        assert request.method == "POST", request.method
+        return reply
+
+    return respond
+
+
+def _deployment(route: str, wire: Wire) -> dict[str, str]:
+    if route == "gemini":
+        return {"model": f"gemini/{_MODEL}", "api_base": wire.url, "api_key": "scripted-key"}
+    return {
+        "model": f"vertex_ai/{_MODEL}",
+        "api_base": wire.url,
+        "vertex_project": _PROJECT,
+        "vertex_location": _LOCATION,
+        "vertex_credentials": service_account_json(_PROJECT, wire.url),
+    }
+
+
+def _text_of(chunk: object) -> str:
+    choices: Final = getattr(chunk, "choices", None) or ()
+    return "".join(str(choice.delta.content or "") for choice in choices)
+
+
+def _complete_sync(route: str, wire: Wire, stream: bool) -> str:
+    response: Final = litellm.completion(
+        **_deployment(route, wire), messages=_MESSAGES, stream=stream, timeout=_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
+    )
+    if stream:
+        return "".join(_text_of(chunk) for chunk in response)
+    return str(response.choices[0].message.content)
+
+
+async def _complete_async(route: str, wire: Wire, stream: bool) -> str:
+    response: Final = await litellm.acompletion(
+        **_deployment(route, wire), messages=_MESSAGES, stream=stream, timeout=_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
+    )
+    if stream:
+        parts: Final = [_text_of(chunk) async for chunk in response]
+        return "".join(parts)
+    return str(response.choices[0].message.content)
+
+

+    if client == "async":
+        return asyncio.run(_complete_async(route, wire, stream))
+    return _complete_sync(route, wire, stream)

+    pool: Final = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)

+

+    with wire_server(_peer(_stream_that_completes())) as wire:

### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

### Bug Description

When using the LiteLLM proxy router with multiple deployments of the same embedding `model_name` across different hosts, failover never occurs when a host is unreachable. The router attempts the selected deployment once, fails, and returns an error — no retries, no failover to other deployments in the model group.

### Root Cause

In `litellm/router.py`, the `aembedding()` method does not set `num_retries` in kwargs before calling `async_function_with_fallbacks()`. Compare `aembedding` to every other router method (`acompletion`, `acreate_file`, `atext_completion`, etc.) which all include this line:

```python
kwargs["num_retries"] = kwargs.get("num_retries", self.num_retries)
```

**`aembedding` (missing the line — bug):**
```python
async def aembedding(self, model, input, is_async=True, **kwargs):
    try:
        kwargs["model"] = model
        kwargs["input"] = input
        kwargs["original_function"] = self._aembedding          # ✓
        # kwargs["num_retries"] = ...                           # ✗ MISSING
        self._update_kwargs_before_fallbacks(model=model, kwargs=kwargs)
        response = await self.async_function_with_fallbacks(**kwargs)
```

**`acreate_file` (correct pattern — for comparison):**
```python
async def acreate_file(self, model, **kwargs):
    try:
        kwargs["model"] = model
        kwargs["original_function"] = self._acreate_file
        kwargs["num_retries"] = kwargs.get("num_retries", self.num_retries)  # ✓ present
        self._update_kwargs_before_fallbacks(model=model, kwargs=kwargs)
        response = await self.async_function_with_fallbacks(**kwargs)
```

Note: `_update_kwargs_before_fallbacks` also sets `num_retries` (line 2234), but it uses `kwargs.get("num_retries", self.num_retries)` — so if `num_retries` is already in kwargs it won't be overwritten. The problem is that `async_function_with_retries` pops `num_retries` from kwargs (line 5564), so on the retry path the key is gone and `_update_kwargs_before_fallbacks` may not re-set it correctly. The result is `num_retries` evaluates to `0` inside the retry loop, causing immediate failure with no retries attempted.

### Fix

Add the missing line to `aembedding()` in `router.py`:

```python
async def aembedding(self, model, input, is_async=True, **kwargs):
    try:
        kwargs["model"] = model
        kwargs["input"] = input
        kwargs["original_function"] = self._aembedding
        kwargs["num_retries"] = kwargs.get("num_retries", self.num_retries)  # ADD THIS
        self._update_kwargs_before_fallbacks(model=model, kwargs=kwargs)
        response = await self.async_function_with_fallbacks(**kwargs)
```



### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure LiteLLM proxy with multiple deployments of the same embedding `model_name`:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: mxbai-embed-large
    litellm_params:
      model: ollama/mxbai-embed-large:latest
      api_base: http://host1:11434

  - model_name: mxbai-embed-large
    litellm_params:
      model: ollama/mxbai-embed-large:latest
      api_base: http://host2:11434

router_settings:
  routing_strategy: simple-shuffle
  num_retries: 3
  allowed_fails: 0
  cooldown_time: 60
```

2. Take `host1` offline
3. Send an embedding request for `mxbai-embed-large`
4. Observe the request fails immediately with no retries — `host2` is never tried
5. Repeat the same test with a chat completion model group — failover works correctly, confirming the bug is specific to `aembedding`

## Additional Context

This bug was discovered while investigating embedding failover in a multi-host Ollama setup. Chat completion failover was working correctly (after separately fixing the `APIConnectionError` cooldown bug — see related issue #27362 ). Embedding failover was still broken despite identical config, and code inspection revealed this missing line as the cause.

All other async router methods set `num_retries` in kwargs before calling `async_function_with_fallbacks`. The `aembedding` method appears to have been overlooked when this pattern was established or when retries were added to other methods.

title: [Bug]: litellm_content_filter evaluations missing from request logs and Guardrails Monitor

judge.reasoning:
Patch A diagnoses the bug as a metadata-bucket merge problem (content filters recording into litellm_metadata while the logging payload takes metadata's list whole) and adds a merge step in get_standard_logging_metadata. The independent tests contradict that diagnosis: every one of the five issue-derived tests fails on base+A with exactly the same assertion as on base (content filters still have no evaluation record, no Monitor index rows, zero Monitor counts). A's first two unit tests only exercise a hand-built split-bucket request and so pass by construction; its end-to-end test runs the real six-guardrail flow, which the independent evidence shows still drops the content filters. A therefore does not fix the reported behavior.

Patch B finds the actual root cause: when message scoping (e.g. skip_system_message) leaves a content filter nothing to scan, the OpenAI chat translation handler never records any guardrail_information, so the guardrail appears in applied_guardrails but not in the persisted evaluation list. B records a `not_run` entry in that path, plumbs the new status through usage tracking (index rows so per-request drill-down finds the request, dedup by name/id), compliance checks, and the UI (badges, counts, timeline). Four of the five independent tests pass on B, including the end-to-end request-log tests for streaming and non-streaming and the Monitor per-request index test. The one remaining failure is the daily request-count test: B deliberately excludes not_run from requests_evaluated, so the daily rollup still shows zero for guardrails that never scanned. That is a defensible design choice (counting a skipped scan as a pass would inflate pass rates) but it leaves part of the issue's Monitor expectation unmet, and the UI/compliance changes are a sizable surface for a bug fix. B's tests cover the new handler behavior with genuine regressions (system-only, null content, image-only, self-recording guardrails) plus tracking, endpoint, compliance and UI cases.

On correctness B clearly wins: it addresses the real cause and makes the issue's primary scenario observable in request logs and Monitor drill-down, while A changes nothing in practice. B's broader scope is coherent with introducing a new status and does not obscure the fix.

title: [Bug]: provider budget never counts embedding or rerank spend — RouterBudgetLimiting raises "custom_llm_provider is required"

judge.reasoning: Both patches make the independent tests pass, so the difference is in where the fix lands and what it leaves behind. The issue's root cause is that embedding(), rerank(), transcription() and speech() resolve custom_llm_provider but never place it into the logging litellm_params, unlike completion(). Patch B fixes exactly that at every producer the issue names (embedding, rerank, transcription, speech) plus the same-shaped image_generation and amoderation sites, placing the key after **kwargs so it cannot be clobbered. This restores the contract that every call type's litellm_params carries the provider, which benefits any other callback reading that field, and it leaves the budget limiter's strict check intact so a future regression is loud rather than silent. Patch A instead changes the consumer to read custom_llm_provider from standard_logging_object and silently skips provider accounting when it is None. That masks the producer-side gap rather than closing it, drops the error signal the issue relied on to discover the bug, and leaves litellm_params still missing the provider for every non-chat surface. Its one real advantage is incidental coverage of responses/anthropic_messages, which the issue did not raise. On tests, Patch A's synthetic-kwargs unit tests are cleaner and more deterministic, while Patch B's Router + respx tests are heavier and poll, but they exercise the actual code paths that were broken (embedding, rerank, transcription, speech, images, moderation) and would fail before the change. Scope and craft are comparable; B's additions are small, uniform, and consistent with how completion() already populates litellm_params. B is the better fix.

issue_md:
### What happened?

With `router_settings.provider_budget_config` enabled, **every** `/v1/embeddings` and `/v1/rerank` call raises inside the budget callback:

```
LiteLLM:ERROR: litellm_logging.py:2672 - LiteLLM.LoggingError: [Non-Blocking] Exception occurred while success logging
  File ".../litellm/litellm_core_utils/litellm_logging.py", line 2618, in async_success_handler
    await callback.async_log_success_event(...)
  File ".../litellm/router_strategy/budget_limiter.py", line 412, in async_log_success_event
    raise ValueError("custom_llm_provider is required")
ValueError: custom_llm_provider is required
```

The error is labelled non-blocking and the request succeeds, so it looks cosmetic. It is not: `RouterBudgetLimiting.async_log_success_event` raises **before** `_increment_spend_for_key`, so **embedding and rerank spend is never added to the provider budget**. The ceiling silently under-counts, and a deployment that is mostly embeddings would never reach it.

`/v1/chat/completions` is unaffected — its spend does accumulate.

### Root cause

`budget_limiter.py:410` reads the provider from `litellm_params`:

```python
custom_llm_provider: str = kwargs.get("litellm_params", {}).get("custom_llm_provider", None)
if custom_llm_provider is None:
    raise ValueError("custom_llm_provider is required")
```

`completion()` puts it there (`main.py:5289`):

```python
litellm_params = get_litellm_params(
    ...
    custom_llm_provider=custom_llm_provider,
    ...
)
```

`embedding()` does not (`main.py:6028`):

```python
litellm_params_dict = get_litellm_params(**kwargs)
```

`custom_llm_provider` is a **named parameter** of `embedding()`, so it is never in `**kwargs`; and it has already been resolved a few lines above by `get_llm_provider()` — it is passed to `logging.update_environment_variables(custom_llm_provider=...)` on the very next statement, just not into `litellm_params`.

Same shape at `main.py:7548` (`transcription`) and `main.py:7825` (`speech`). `rerank_api/main.py:168` builds `rerank_litellm_params` without it as well.

Because the parameter is consumed by the function signature, **no configuration can work around this** — passing `custom_llm_provider` in the request body or in the deployment's `litellm_params` still ends up as the named argument, never in `**kwargs`.

### Relevant log output

Reproduced 3/3 on `/v1/embeddings` and `/v1/rerank`; 0/4 on `/v1/chat/completions` (streaming and non-streaming, cache hit and miss).

`GET /provider/budgets` on the same proxy shows spend accumulating from chat only:

```json
{"providers":{"bedrock":{"budget_limit":1000.0,"time_period":"1mo","spend":159.18631146,...}}}
```

### Suggested fix

Pass the already-resolved value, as `completion()` does:

```python
litellm_params_dict = get_litellm_params(custom_llm_provider=custom_llm_provider, **kwargs)
```

### Config

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: titan-embed-v2
    litellm_params:
      model: bedrock/amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0
      aws_region_name: us-east-1
  - model_name: cohere-rerank-v3-5
    litellm_params:
      model: bedrock/arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1::foundation-model/cohere.rerank-v3-5:0
      aws_region_name: us-east-1

router_settings:
  provider_budget_config:
    bedrock:
      budget_limit: 1000
      time_period: 1mo
  redis_host: os.environ/REDIS_HOST
```

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_

title: [Bug]: /v1/models never expands litellm_proxy/* wildcards — provider-endpoint discovery is gated on a static dict that excludes litellm_proxy

judge.reasoning: Both patches fix the root cause identified in the issue: `get_provider_models` returning None before discovery is attempted for providers absent from the static `models_by_provider` catalog. Both admit providers that have a registered model-info config via `ProviderConfigManager.get_provider_model_info`, and all three independent tests pass on both. The difference is in how the gate is shaped. Patch B implements exactly the issue's suggested fix: discovery is admitted only when `litellm.check_provider_endpoint` is on, isolated in a small, documented helper `_supports_provider_endpoint_discovery`. Patch A drops the `check_provider_endpoint` condition entirely, so any provider with a model-info config now routes through `get_valid_models` even when discovery is off, changing the return value from None to [] for those providers. Patch A's own test documents this as a deliberate behavioral change, and it is probably harmless downstream, but it is a wider change than the issue asks for and relies on `get_valid_models` honoring the global flag internally rather than the gate doing so explicitly. Patch A's test for the discovery-off case also depends on the global `check_provider_endpoint` default rather than monkeypatching it, which is a minor fragility. On tests, Patch B's end-to-end test is stronger: it flushes the model cache, drives the real `LiteLLMProxyChatConfig.get_models` path by stubbing the HTTP client, and asserts the exact upstream URL and Authorization header built from the deployment's api_base/api_key, matching the issue's expectation that discovery uses the wildcard deployment's credentials. It also adds a hosted_vllm case and a negative test proving no upstream request is made when discovery is off. Patch A's test patches `OpenAIGPTConfig.get_models` at the base class, which verifies the credentials reach the fetcher but exercises less of the real path. Scope and craft favor B: it stays within the issue's ask, names and documents the new condition clearly, and keeps the original control flow intact.

issue_md:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

In a chained setup (LiteLLM in front of LiteLLM) using the documented wildcard config for the `litellm_proxy` provider with `check_provider_endpoint: true`, the downstream proxy's `GET /v1/models` returns the literal string `litellm_proxy/*` as its only model entry instead of the upstream's expanded model list. It fails silently: no HTTP request to the upstream is made and nothing is logged. Routing is unaffected — `model: litellm_proxy/<name>` requests forward to the upstream correctly — so only discovery is broken.

**Expected:** one `litellm_proxy/<name>` entry per model listed by the upstream, discovered via the wildcard deployment's `api_base`/`api_key`, as described in the [model discovery docs](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/model_discovery), which list LiteLLM Proxy as a supported provider.

**Root cause (from the source, `main` @ `6e569ee0`):** `get_provider_models` in `litellm/proxy/auth/model_checks.py` gates provider-endpoint discovery on membership in the static `litellm.models_by_provider` dict:

```python
if provider in litellm.models_by_provider:
    provider_models = get_valid_models(custom_llm_provider=provider, litellm_params=litellm_params)
    return provider_models
return None
```

`litellm_proxy` is not a key in that dict (`litellm/__init__.py`, `_build_models_by_provider()`), so the function returns `None` before discovery is attempted, and `get_known_models_from_wildcard` silently returns `[]`. The wildcard-expansion path upstream of this point works correctly — `_get_wildcard_models` finds the deployment and extracts its `litellm_params` — and the provider's model-list fetcher exists and works (`LiteLLMProxyChatConfig.get_models()`, registered in `ProviderConfigManager.get_provider_model_info`), but it is unreachable through this gate. The effect is ironic: the providers that most need endpoint discovery (`litellm_proxy`, `hosted_vllm` — dynamic model lists with no static catalog) are exactly the ones a static-catalog membership test excludes. Setting `LITELLM_PROXY_API_BASE`/`LITELLM_PROXY_API_KEY` does not help this path; the code returns before credentials are consulted.

**Suggested fix:** admit providers that have a registered model-info config when `check_provider_endpoint` is enabled, rather than requiring membership in the static catalog:

```python
if provider in litellm.models_by_provider or (
    litellm.check_provider_endpoint
    and ProviderConfigManager.get_provider_model_info(model=None, provider=LlmProviders(provider)) is not None
):
    return get_valid_models(custom_llm_provider=provider, litellm_params=litellm_params)
```

This fixes the same class of failure for any dynamically-listed provider, not just `litellm_proxy`.

Closest existing issues, none of which cover this: #13643 — same symptom family, stale-closed without a fix; #20064 — open, one comment describes this exact chained-proxy case; #13078 — closed "unable to repro", but the repro attempt used an `openai` config while the reporter hit it with `litellm_proxy`/`hosted_vllm`; #36945 — same symptom, different cause (`STORE_MODEL_IN_DB` drops the flag), for `vertex_ai`; #28264 — discovery failing to resolve stored `litellm_credential_name` credentials, fixed by #28419 (that fix is present and doesn't help here — this bug bails out before credentials are consulted at all); #31856 — open PR fixing the sibling gate for `custom_openai` only; #11784 — fixed a different variant.

### User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer whose app lists models from a chained LLM gateway (a downstream LiteLLM proxy forwarding to a central upstream LiteLLM proxy) sees only a wildcard string instead of usable model names, so their model picker is broken.

1. The developer sends GET http://litellm-downstream:4000/v1/models with their gateway key
2. The response's `data` array contains a single entry whose id is the literal string `litellm_proxy/*` — not a callable model name — no matter how many models the upstream serves
3. Their client app's model picker, which populates from that endpoint, shows only `litellm_proxy/*`; picking it fails, and the developer has to learn real model names out-of-band
4. If the developer already knows a name, POST http://litellm-downstream:4000/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "litellm_proxy/gpt-4o"` works — the request forwards through to the upstream and on to the provider

After a (hypothetical) fix: the same gateway's model list shows every model the upstream serves, so the picker just works.

1. The developer sends GET http://litellm-downstream:4000/v1/models with their gateway key
2. The response's `data` array contains one entry per upstream model — e.g. `litellm_proxy/gpt-4o`, `litellm_proxy/claude-sonnet`
3. Their client app's model picker shows those names; the developer picks one
4. POST http://litellm-downstream:4000/v1/chat/completions with the picked name works exactly as before

### Proof the bug occurs

Version: **v1.98.0** (pip `litellm[proxy]==1.98.0`), locally on Linux, no database.

Config the upstream proxy ran with (`upstream.yaml`, port 4010):

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gpt-4o
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o
      api_key: sk-fake-upstream-provider-key
  - model_name: claude-sonnet
    litellm_params:
      model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5
      api_key: sk-fake-upstream-provider-key

general_settings:
  master_key: sk-upstream-1234
```

Config the downstream proxy ran with (`downstream.yaml`, port 4020), no extra env vars:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: "litellm_proxy/*"
    litellm_params:
      model: "litellm_proxy/*"
      api_base: http://127.0.0.1:4010
      api_key: sk-upstream-1234

litellm_settings:
  check_provider_endpoint: true

general_settings:
  master_key: sk-downstream-1234
```

Started with `litellm --config upstream.yaml --port 4010` and `litellm --config downstream.yaml --port 4020`.

The upstream lists its models fine:

```
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4010/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-upstream-1234"
{"data":[{"id":"gpt-4o","object":"model","created":1677610602,"owned_by":"openai","mode":"chat","max_input_tokens":128000,"max_output_tokens":16384},{"id":"claude-sonnet","object":"model","created":1677610602,"owned_by":"openai"}],"object":"list"}
```

The downstream returns only the literal wildcard — this is the bug:

```
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4020/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-downstream-1234"
{"data":[{"id":"litellm_proxy/*","object":"model","created":1677610602,"owned_by":"openai"}],"object":"list"}
```

Routing through the same chain works (the request traverses downstream → upstream → OpenAI's real API, which rejects the deliberately fake provider key — proving the forwarding path is fully functional):

```
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4020/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-downstream-1234" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"litellm_proxy/gpt-4o","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
{"error":{"message":"litellm.AuthenticationError: Error code: 401 - {'error': {'message': 'litellm.AuthenticationError: AuthenticationError: OpenAIException - Incorrect API key provided: sk-fake-*****************-key. ...'}}. Received Model Group=litellm_proxy/gpt-4o\nAvailable Model Group Fallbacks=None","type":null,"param":null,"code":"401"}}
```

During the `/v1/models` request the upstream's access log shows no incoming request — the discovery fetch is never attempted.

**Workaround confirming the diagnosis:** the only change below is adding `infer_model_from_keys: true` and the two env vars — this reaches the same provider fetcher through the env-inference path, which does not go through the `models_by_provider` gate:

```yaml
general_settings:
  master_key: sk-downstream-1234
  infer_model_from_keys: true
```

```
$ LITELLM_PROXY_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:4010 LITELLM_PROXY_API_KEY=sk-upstream-1234 \
    litellm --config downstream-workaround.yaml --port 4020
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4020/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-downstream-1234"
{"data":[{"id":"litellm_proxy/*","object":"model","created":1677610602,"owned_by":"openai"},{"id":"litellm_proxy/gpt-4o","object":"model","created":1677610602,"owned_by":"openai","mode":"chat","max_input_tokens":128000,"max_output_tokens":16384},{"id":"litellm_proxy/claude-sonnet","object":"model","created":1677610602,"owned_by":"openai"}],"object":"list"}
```

(The literal `litellm_proxy/*` entry still leaking into the successful listing is the separate known issue being addressed in #29165/#36398.)

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.98.0

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_

title: [Bug]: Bedrock Realtime hides provider throttles as normal WebSocket closes and lacks disconnect cleanup

judge.reasoning: Patch B addresses both halves of the issue; Patch A addresses only the slot-cleanup half. B adds a throttle classifier (`realtime_failure_classification`) that maps 429 / RouterRateLimitError (following `__cause__` through the committed-session replay refusal) to a `rate_limit_error` Realtime error event and a 1013 close, remaps Bedrock `ServiceQuotaExceededException` from 400 to 429 so the router cools down and falls back, and stores the committed error in scope so a post-readiness throttle stays retryable. A does none of this: the client still receives `server_error`/1011 for a throttle, and the two independent 'throttle without fallback' tests fail on A exactly as on base. On cleanup, B makes idempotency a property of the limiter itself (claim `stash.parallel_slot = None` before awaiting the release in all four release paths) and wraps the route's release in a shielded, exception-swallowing helper applied to the pre-call rejection, the normal finally, and the responses websocket. A instead relies on success/failure stamps set by callers to decide whether the route may release, which is fragile (any path that dispatches a callback without stamping double-releases) and leaves the underlying race unaddressed; its shielding is also absent, so a cancelled session can still skip release. A's switch from FIRST_EXCEPTION to FIRST_COMPLETED is a reasonable fix for client-disconnect hang but is incidental. Tests: B adds handler tests proving no `session.updated` before readiness, 429 propagation, fallback replay, and a limiter race test plus end-to-end route tests using the real v3 limiter with max_parallel_requests=1 for every exit path the issue lists. A's tests cover stamp ownership and slot release but not the throttle signaling. The independent suite confirms: B passes all 10, A fails the 2 throttle-classification tests. B's extra touch on /v1/responses is adjacent but low risk and does not obscure the fix.

# [Bug]: Bedrock Realtime hides provider throttles as normal WebSocket closes and lacks disconnect cleanup

### Check for existing issues

- [x] I searched the existing issues and did not find one covering Bedrock Nova Sonic throttling and request-slot cleanup on `/v1/realtime`.

### What happened?

When Bedrock's regional concurrent-session quota is exhausted, LiteLLM acknowledges the throttled Nova Sonic session as ready, emits no Realtime `error` event, and closes the client WebSocket with code `1000` and an empty reason.

This makes a capacity rejection indistinguishable from a successful, intentional session close. The application cannot identify a retryable throttle, apply backoff, fail over before sending audio, or report an actionable error.

There is also no WebSocket-lifecycle cleanup around the proxy's `/v1/realtime` route. Pre-call processing acquires proxy rate-limit state, including `max_parallel_requests` slots, but unlike the SSE streaming path the Realtime endpoint has no shielded `finally` that calls `_arelease_max_parallel_requests_on_disconnect`. When a WebSocket is cancelled or a provider failure is suppressed before a normal LiteLLM success/failure callback, the slot can remain until the limiter's one-hour TTL prunes it.

The Bedrock handler currently suppresses forwarding failures and then performs a normal close:

```python
# litellm/llms/bedrock/realtime/handler.py
await asyncio.gather(
    client_to_bedrock_task,
    bedrock_to_client_task,
    return_exceptions=True,
)

...

except Exception as e:
    verbose_proxy_logger.debug(
        "Bedrock to client forwarding ended: %s", e, exc_info=True
    )
finally:
    await client_ws.close()
```

Because `client_ws.close()` has no error code or reason, Starlette sends a normal WebSocket close. Because the forwarding exception does not escape, the router cannot classify the attempt as throttled, update deployment health/cooldown state, or attempt an ordered deployment fallback before the session is committed.

Expected behavior:

1. A Bedrock throttling or service-quota exception before provider readiness is propagated to the router as one logical failure.
2. If another deployment is configured, LiteLLM attempts that deployment before acknowledging the session as ready.
3. If no fallback is available, the client receives a Realtime `error` event containing a stable, retryable throttle classification, followed by an error close such as `1013` (try again later) or `1011`, not `1000`.
4. `session.updated` is emitted only after the provider has accepted the session configuration and is ready to receive audio.
5. Every WebSocket exit path releases exactly the proxy concurrency slot acquired for that session: normal completion, client disconnect, provider failure, cancellation, and pre-readiness fallback.
6. Cleanup is idempotent so a logging callback and disconnect cleanup cannot double-decrement the limiter.

### User flow

1. Twenty clients establish Nova Sonic sessions in an AWS account/region whose concurrent-request quota is 20.
2. A twenty-first client connects to LiteLLM and sends `session.update`.
3. LiteLLM sends `session.created` and `session.updated`, so the client reasonably begins sending audio.
4. Bedrock rejects that session because capacity is exhausted.
5. LiteLLM emits no `error` event and closes with `1000`, reason `""`.
6. The client cannot distinguish this from a clean end-of-session and has no reliable throttle signal on which to base retry or failover behavior.

After a fix, step 3 does not occur until upstream readiness is established. A rejected attempt either falls back before audio is accepted or produces an explicit retryable error and non-normal close, and its concurrency slot is released immediately.

### Proof the bug occurs

The reproduction used the deployed LiteLLM proxy, a team-scoped virtual key, and real Bedrock Nova 2 Sonic sessions. No mock provider was used.

Environment:

```text
LiteLLM: v1.98.0
Commit: d8f71d7bdbd7c9873d98293f83d64c6db72847e6
Endpoint: /v1/realtime
Provider/model: Bedrock amazon.nova-2-sonic-v1:0
Region: us-east-1
Proxy replicas: 4
AWS Bedrock quota code: L-995EBD81
AWS concurrent-session quota: 20
```

The test opened 21 concurrent sessions and continued reading each socket for 10 seconds after `session.updated`.

Observed client result:

```text
21/21 sessions received session.updated
20/21 sessions remained connected for the hold period
1/21 sessions closed after readiness
close code: 1000
close reason: ""
Realtime error event: none
```

CloudWatch for the exact test minute showed:

```text
AWS/Bedrock Invocations = 20
AWS/Bedrock InvocationThrottles = 1
```

The alternate `us-west-2` deployment received no invocation, despite being registered under the same model group with lower routing priority.

The observed normal close follows directly from the handler source quoted above. The cleanup concern follows from the proxy lifecycle:

- `common_processing_pre_call_logic()` runs before routing and invokes the proxy limiter hooks.
- The v3 parallel limiter stores each acquired slot and gives it a 3,600-second TTL.
- LiteLLM already provides `ProxyLogging._arelease_max_parallel_requests_on_disconnect()` and uses it from shielded SSE cleanup when no logging callback owns the release.
- The `/v1/realtime` route has only `try`/`except` around routing; it has no corresponding `finally` cleanup.
- The Bedrock forwarding coroutines suppress exceptions, so the outer route can return without a failure callback that would otherwise release/account for the request.

Suggested regression coverage:

1. Make the Bedrock duplex output raise a throttling exception while applying the first `session.update`.
2. Assert `session.updated` has not been sent.
3. With a second deployment configured, assert the exception reaches the router and the retained configuration is attempted there.
4. Without a fallback, assert a Realtime `error` event and non-normal close are sent with a retryable throttle classification.
5. Configure a virtual key with `max_parallel_requests=1`, connect and disconnect normally, and assert another session can immediately acquire the slot.
6. Repeat step 5 for client cancellation, pre-readiness throttle, provider failure after readiness, and proxy task cancellation.
7. Assert every acquired slot is released exactly once and no path waits for the 3,600-second TTL.
8. Assert CloudWatch/provider throttles become LiteLLM deployment failures rather than successful sessions.

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on?

v1.98.0

+"""
+/v1/realtime session exits: provider throttles reach the client as a retryable
+error (not a normal 1000 close), and every exit path frees the key's
+max_parallel_requests slot right away instead of leaving it to the limiter's
+one-hour TTL.
+
+The sessions run through the real realtime_websocket_endpoint and a real v3
+parallel request limiter with max_parallel_requests=1; only pre-call wiring and
+the routed provider call are faked. "The slot was released" is checked the way
+a client would see it: a second session's admission succeeds.
+"""
+
+import asyncio
+import json
+from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
+from typing import Final
+from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, MagicMock, patch
+
+import pytest
+from fastapi import HTTPException
+
+from litellm.caching.caching import DualCache
+from litellm.llms.bedrock.common_utils import BedrockError
+from litellm.proxy import proxy_server as ps
+from litellm.proxy._types import UserAPIKeyAuth
+from litellm.proxy.hooks.parallel_request_limiter_v3 import (
+    _PROXY_MaxParallelRequestsHandler_v3,
+)
+from litellm.proxy.utils import InternalUsageCache, hash_token
+from litellm.types.router import RouterRateLimitError
+
+MODEL: Final = "bedrock/amazon.nova-2-sonic-v1:0"
+
+
+def _fake_websocket() -> MagicMock:
+    ws = MagicMock()
+    ws.headers = {}
+    ws.scope = {"headers": [], "type": "websocket"}
+    ws.url = "ws://testserver/v1/realtime"
+    ws.accept = AsyncMock()
+    ws.send_text = AsyncMock()
+    ws.close = AsyncMock()
+    return ws
+
+
+class _Session:
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.cache: Final = DualCache()
+        self.limiter: Final = _PROXY_MaxParallelRequestsHandler_v3(internal_usage_cache=InternalUsageCache(self.cache))
+        self.user_api_key_dict: Final = UserAPIKeyAuth(
+            api_key=hash_token("sk-realtime-session"), token="hashed-token", max_parallel_requests=1
+        )
+
+    async def admit(self, data: dict) -> None:
+        await self.limiter.async_pre_call_hook(
+            user_api_key_dict=self.user_api_key_dict, cache=self.cache, data=data, call_type="_arealtime"
+        )
+
+    async def run(
+        self,
+        llm_call: Callable[[], Awaitable[None]],
+        *,
+        ws: MagicMock | None = None,
+        fail_after_admission: Exception | None = None,
+    ) -> MagicMock:
+        """Run one realtime session in its own task, as the ASGI server does per connection."""
+        websocket: Final = ws if ws is not None else _fake_websocket()
+        logging_obj: Final = MagicMock()
+        logging_obj.model_call_details = {}
+
+        async def pre_call(*_args: object, **kwargs: object):
+            data: Final = {"model": MODEL}
+            await self.admit(data)
+            if fail_after_admission is not None:
+                raise fail_after_admission
+            return data, logging_obj
+
+        async def route_request(**_kwargs: object):
+            return llm_call()
+
+        with (
+            patch.object(
+                ps, "can_key_call_resolved_model", new=AsyncMock()
+            ),  # test-quality-ok: no HTTP boundary; key/model access is not under test
+            patch.object(
+                ps.ProxyBaseLLMRequestProcessing, "common_processing_pre_call_logic", new=pre_call
+            ),  # test-quality-ok: pre-call runs the real limiter admission
+            patch.object(
+                ps, "route_request", new=route_request
+            ),  # test-quality-ok: fakes the provider relay whose exit is under test
+            patch.object(
+                ps.proxy_logging_obj,
+                "get_proxy_hook",
+                new=lambda name: self.limiter if name == "parallel_request_limiter" else None,
+            ),  # test-quality-ok: wires the real limiter in place of the proxy's configured hooks
+        ):
+            await asyncio.create_task(
+                ps.realtime_websocket_endpoint(
+                    websocket=websocket,
+                    model=MODEL,
+                    intent=None,
+                    guardrails=None,
+                    user_api_key_dict=self.user_api_key_dict,
+                )
+            )
+        return websocket
+
+    async def assert_slot_is_free(self) -> None:
+        async def admit_next() -> None:
+            await self.admit({"model": MODEL})
+
+        # A fresh task has a fresh request stash, like the next client connection.
+        await asyncio.create_task(admit_next())
+
+
+async def _completes() -> None:
+    return None
+
+
+def _raises(error: BaseException) -> Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]:
+    async def call() -> None:
+        raise error
+
+    return call
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_slot_is_held_while_a_session_is_open():
+    """Guards the other assertions: an open session really does hold the only slot."""
+    session: Final = _Session()
+    opened: Final = asyncio.Event()
+
+    async def stays_open() -> None:
+        opened.set()
+        await asyncio.Event().wait()
+
+    task: Final = asyncio.create_task(session.run(stays_open))
+    await opened.wait()
+    with pytest.raises(HTTPException) as rejected:
+        await session.assert_slot_is_free()
+    assert rejected.value.status_code == 429
+    task.cancel()
+    with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError):
+        await task
+    await session.assert_slot_is_free()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_bedrock_throttle_reaches_the_client_as_a_retryable_error_close():
+    session: Final = _Session()
+    throttle: Final = BedrockError(status_code=429, message="ThrottlingException: Too many concurrent requests")
+
+    ws: Final = await session.run(_raises(throttle))
+
+    event: Final = json.loads(ws.send_text.await_args.args[0])
+    assert event["type"] == "error"
+    assert event["error"]["type"] == "rate_limit_error"
+    assert "ThrottlingException" in event["error"]["message"]
+    assert ws.close.await_args.kwargs["code"] == 1013
+    await session.assert_slot_is_free()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_all_deployments_cooled_down_after_throttles_is_a_retryable_error_close():
+    session: Final = _Session()
+    cooled_down: Final = RouterRateLimitError(
+        model=MODEL, cooldown_time=5, enable_pre_call_checks=False, cooldown_list=["a", "b"], model_ids=["a", "b"]
+    )
+
+    ws: Final = await session.run(_raises(cooled_down))
+
+    assert json.loads(ws.send_text.await_args.args[0])["error"]["type"] == "rate_limit_error"
+    assert ws.close.await_args.kwargs["code"] == 1013
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_provider_failure_after_readiness_is_a_server_error_close_and_frees_the_slot():
+    session: Final = _Session()
+
+    ws: Final = await session.run(_raises(BedrockError(status_code=424, message="ModelStreamErrorException: broke")))
+
+    assert json.loads(ws.send_text.await_args.args[0])["error"]["type"] == "server_error"
+    assert ws.close.await_args.kwargs["code"] == 1011
+    await session.assert_slot_is_free()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_normal_session_end_frees_the_slot():
+    session: Final = _Session()
+
+    ws: Final = await session.run(_completes)
+
+    ws.send_text.assert_not_awaited()
+    await session.assert_slot_is_free()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_cancelled_session_task_frees_the_slot():
+    """A client cancel or proxy shutdown cancels the session task mid-relay; no
+    logging callback fires, so the endpoint's shielded cleanup must release."""
+    session: Final = _Session()
+    relaying: Final = asyncio.Event()
+
+    async def relay_until_cancelled() -> None:
+        relaying.set()
+        await asyncio.Event().wait()
+
+    task: Final = asyncio.create_task(session.run(relay_until_cancelled))
+    await relaying.wait()
+    task.cancel()
+    with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError):
+        await task
+
+    await session.assert_slot_is_free()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_pre_call_failure_after_admission_frees_the_slot():
+    """A guardrail or later hook failing after the limiter admitted the session
+    rejects it before routing; that slot must not wait for the TTL either."""
+    session: Final = _Session()
+
+    ws: Final = await session.run(_completes, fail_after_admission=Exception("blocked by guardrail"))
+
+    ws.close.assert_awaited_once_with(code=1011, reason="Pre-call error")
+    await session.assert_slot_is_free()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_slot_released_by_the_logging_callback_is_not_released_again():
+    """The limiter's own logging callback already freed the slot (e.g. the
+    session's failure was logged); the endpoint cleanup must then be a no-op
+    rather than decrement another session's slot."""
+    session: Final = _Session()
+    release: Final = AsyncMock(wraps=session.limiter._release_parallel_request_slots)
+
+    async def logged_then_ends() -> None:
+        await session.limiter.async_log_failure_event(kwargs={}, response_obj=None, start_time=None, end_time=None)
+
+    with patch.object(
+        session.limiter, "_release_parallel_request_slots", new=release
+    ):  # test-quality-ok: counts releases on the real limiter
+        await session.run(logged_then_ends)
+
+    assert release.await_count == 1
+    await session.assert_slot_is_free()

title: [Bug]: openai dependency still pinned to <3.0.0 in latest release, blocks packages requiring openai>=3.0.0

judge.reasoning: Both patches make the identical manifest change (openai<4.0.0 in both pyproject.toml files), so the independent tests cannot distinguish them; the difference is whether the loosened pin is actually safe. Patch A only edits the specifier and adds tests that read the TOML back and assert the string admits 3.x, which is tautological and proves nothing about runtime compatibility. The issue author merely speculates the ceiling 'appears to be stale'; nothing in Patch A verifies that. Patch B's runtime changes show the ceiling was not stale: openai 3.x ships its own Timeout type, DefaultHttpxClient/DefaultAsyncHttpxClient backed by a different http module (httpx2), an SDK Response type for HttpxBinaryResponseContent, and a DefaultHttpx2Client in workload identity. Patch B adapts litellm for these differences (CompletionTimeout.normalize, router field_validator, exceptions accepting non-httpx responses, SDK clients constructed with an httpx-based http_client so litellm's exception mapping and timeout plumbing keep working, proxy audio_speech no longer reaching into response.response.headers directly), and critically adds a CI matrix that installs openai 2.20.0, 3.0.0 and 3.25.0 and runs the affected suites plus a pyright type check against each. Its unit tests are parametrized over both http backends and would fail on 3.x without the code changes. Under Patch A, a user who installs litellm with openai 3.x would get a resolvable lock but likely runtime breakage, which merely moves the failure later. On scope, Patch B is very large and the 1600+ lines of integration/chaos tests (worker SIGKILL, upstream SIGSTOP) go well beyond the ask, and the __del__ hooks on the new client classes are a mild risk, but that excess is mostly test code and does not obscure the fix. Patch B resolves the issue at its root (make litellm genuinely compatible with the range it declares) with real tests; Patch A masks the symptom.

issue_md:
### What Happened

`litellm`'s `pyproject.toml` pins `openai>=2.20.0,<3.0.0` even in the latest
release (1.100.0). This makes it impossible to install `litellm` alongside
any package that requires `openai>=3.0.0`.

`openai`'s v3.x line has been on PyPI for a while now (currently 3.9.0), so
the `<3.0.0` ceiling appears to be stale rather than an active compatibility
guard.

### Reproduction

In a project that depends on both `litellm==1.99.0` (or 1.100.0) and another
package requiring `openai>=3.0.0`, `uv lock` fails to resolve:

```
× No solution found when resolving dependencies for split (markers:
│ python_full_version == '3.14.7' and sys_platform == 'win32'):
╰─▶ Because some-package[openai]==X.Y.Z depends on openai>=3.0.0 and
    litellm==1.99.0 depends on openai>=2.20.0,<3.0.0, we can conclude that
    litellm==1.99.0 and some-package[openai]==X.Y.Z are incompatible.
    And because llm depends on litellm==1.99.0, we can conclude that llm and
    some-package[openai]==X.Y.Z are incompatible.
    And because llm depends on some-package[openai]==X.Y.Z and your
    workspace requires llm[all], we can conclude that your workspace's
    requirements are unsatisfiable.
```

+def _error_message(response: httpx.Response) -> str:
+    body: Final = JSON_OBJECT.validate_json(response.content)
+    if "error" in body:
+        return string_value(object_value(body["error"])["message"])
+    detail: Final = body["detail"]
+    if isinstance(detail, str):
+        return detail
+    assert isinstance(detail, list) and detail, response.text
+    return string_value(object_value(detail[0])["msg"])

+        seconds=WORKER_SYNC_SECONDS + 10,
+    )
+
+
+def _attempt(call: Callable[[], _R]) -> _R | openai.APIStatusError:
+    try:
+        return call()
+    except openai.APIStatusError as error:
+        return error
+
+
+def _unknown_to_the_serving_worker(outcome: object) -> bool:
+    return isinstance(outcome, openai.BadRequestError) and "Invalid model name" in outcome.response.text
+
+
+def _outcome_after_worker_sync(call: Callable[[], _R]) -> _R | openai.APIStatusError:
+    return eventually(
+        lambda: _attempt(call),
+        lambda outcome: not _unknown_to_the_serving_worker(outcome),
+        seconds=WORKER_SYNC_SECONDS + 10,
+    )
+
+
+def _after_worker_sync(call: Callable[[], _R]) -> _R:
+    outcome: Final = _outcome_after_worker_sync(call)
+    assert not isinstance(outcome, openai.APIStatusError), outcome.response.text
+    return outcome
+
+
+def _async_after_worker_sync(gateway: Gateway, call: Callable[[openai.AsyncOpenAI], Awaitable[_R]]) -> _R:
+    return _after_worker_sync(lambda: _async_openai(gateway, call))
+

+def _streamed_file_content(gateway: Gateway, file_id: str, model: str) -> tuple[int, tuple[bytes, ...]]:
+    with gateway.client.stream(
+        "GET",
+        f"/v1/files/{file_id}/content",
+        params={"model": model},
+        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {gateway.key}"},
+    ) as response:
+        return response.status_code, tuple(response.iter_bytes())
+
+
+def _upstream_id(managed: str, prefix: str) -> str:
+    encoded: Final = managed.removeprefix(prefix)
+    try:
+        decoded: Final = base64.urlsafe_b64decode(encoded + "=" * (-len(encoded) % 4)).decode()
+    except (binascii.Error, UnicodeDecodeError):
+        return managed
+    return decoded.removeprefix("litellm:").split(";", 1)[0] if decoded.startswith("litellm:") else managed
+
+
+def _spend_row(identity: str) -> Mapping[str, JsonValue]:
+    rows: Final = eventually(
+        lambda: read_rows(
+            'SELECT request_id, call_type, model FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" WHERE request_id = %s', (identity,)
+        ),
+        lambda rows: len(rows) == 1,
+        seconds=70,
+    )
+    return rows[0]
+
+
+def _spend_row_keyed_by_any(identities: frozenset[str]) -> Mapping[str, JsonValue]:
+    keys: Final = tuple(sorted(identities))
+    placeholders: Final = ", ".join("%s" for _ in keys)
+    rows: Final = eventually(
+        lambda: read_rows(
+            f'SELECT request_id, call_type, model FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" WHERE request_id IN ({placeholders})', keys
+        ),
+        lambda rows: len(rows) == 1,
+        seconds=70,
+    )
+    return rows[0]
+
+
+def _spend_request_ids(identities: tuple[str, str, str]) -> frozenset[str]:
+    rows: Final = eventually(
+        lambda: read_rows('SELECT request_id FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" WHERE request_id IN (%s, %s, %s)', identities),
+        lambda rows: len(rows) == 3,
+        seconds=70,
+    )
+    return frozenset(string_value(row["request_id"]) for row in rows)
+
+
+def _anthropic_text(event: RawMessageStreamEvent) -> str:
+    if isinstance(event, RawContentBlockDeltaEvent) and isinstance(event.delta, TextDelta):
+        return event.delta.text
+    return ""
+
+
+def _chunk_text(chunk: ChatCompletionChunk) -> str:
+    return chunk.choices[0].delta.content or "" if chunk.choices else ""
+
+
+def _chunk_finished(chunk: ChatCompletionChunk) -> bool:
+    return bool(chunk.choices) and chunk.choices[0].finish_reason == "stop"
+
+
+def _new_model(gateway: Gateway, api_base: str, timeout: JsonValue) -> httpx.Response:
+    return gateway.request(
+        "POST",
+        "/model/new",
+        {
+            "model_name": f"integration-{uuid.uuid4().hex}",
+            "litellm_params": {
+                "model": f"openai/{UPSTREAM_MODEL}",
+                "api_key": PROVIDER_KEY,
+                "api_base": api_base,
+                "timeout": timeout,
+            },
+            "model_info": {},
+        },
+    )
+

+def _register_accepted_model(scenario: Scenario, response: httpx.Response, shape: str) -> None:
+    assert response.status_code == 200, (shape, response.status_code, response.text)
+    identity: Final = string_value(object_value(JSON_OBJECT.validate_json(response.content)["model_info"])["id"])
+    scenario.cleanups.callback(scenario.delete_model, identity)

+    kind: _Kind

+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class _Completed:

+    anthropic: Anthropic

+class _Observations:
+    def __init__(self, url: str) -> None:
+        self.url = url.rstrip("/")
+        self.items: tuple[Mapping[str, JsonValue], ...] = ()
+
+    def read(self) -> tuple[Mapping[str, JsonValue], ...]:
+        with httpx.Client(timeout=10, trust_env=False) as client:
+            payload: Final = JSON_OBJECT.validate_python(client.get(f"{self.url}/__observations").json())
+        requests: Final = payload.get("requests")
+        assert isinstance(requests, list)
+        self.items = (*self.items, *(object_value(item) for item in requests if isinstance(item, dict)))
+        return self.items

+def _register(
+    scenario: Scenario, upstream_url: str, label: str, response: RoutedResponse | SseResponse
+) -> ScenarioHandle:
+    handle: Final = register_scenario(f"chaos-{label}-{uuid.uuid4().hex}", response, control_url=upstream_url)
+    scenario.cleanups.callback(delete_scenario, handle)
+    return handle

+def _deployments(scenario: Scenario, upstream_url: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
+    plain_handle: Final = _register(scenario, upstream_url, "plain", _PLAIN)
+    stream_handle: Final = _register(scenario, upstream_url, "stream", _STREAM)
+    return (
+        scenario.model(api_base=plain_handle.api_base(), api_key=plain_handle.scenario_id),
+        scenario.model(api_base=stream_handle.api_base(), api_key=stream_handle.scenario_id),

+def _clients(gateway: Gateway, deployments: tuple[str, str]) -> _Clients:
+    base: Final = str(gateway.client.base_url).rstrip("/")
+    clients: Final = _Clients(
+        openai=OpenAI(base_url=f"{base}/v1", api_key=gateway.key, max_retries=0),
+        anthropic=Anthropic(base_url=base, api_key=gateway.key, max_retries=0),
+        plain_model=deployments[0],
+        stream_model=deployments[1],
+    )
+    _import_lazy_sdk_resources_on_this_thread(clients)
+    return clients

+def _import_lazy_sdk_resources_on_this_thread(clients: _Clients) -> None:
+    resources: Final = (
+        clients.openai.chat.completions,
+        clients.openai.completions,
+        clients.openai.responses,
+        clients.openai.moderations,
+        clients.anthropic.messages,
+    )
+    assert all(resource is not None for resource in resources)
+
+
+def _invoke(clients: _Clients, call: _Call) -> str:
+    match call.kind:
+        case "chat":
+            return clients.openai.chat.completions.create(
+                model=clients.plain_model, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": call.marker}], extra_body=_NO_CACHE
+            ).id
+        case "chat_stream":
+            chunks: Final = tuple(
+                clients.openai.chat.completions.create(
+                    model=clients.stream_model,
+                    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": call.marker}],
+                    stream=True,
+                    extra_body=_NO_CACHE,
+                )
+            )
+            assert chunks[-1].choices[0].finish_reason == "stop", chunks
+            assert len({chunk.id for chunk in chunks}) == 1, chunks
+            return chunks[0].id
+        case "messages":
+            return clients.anthropic.messages.create(
+                model=clients.plain_model,
+                max_tokens=64,
+                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": call.marker}],
+                extra_body=_NO_CACHE,
+            ).id
+        case "responses":
+            return clients.openai.responses.create(
+                model=clients.plain_model, input=call.marker, extra_body=_NO_CACHE
+            ).id
+        case "completions":
+            return clients.openai.completions.create(
+                model=clients.plain_model, prompt=call.marker, extra_body=_NO_CACHE
+            ).id
+        case "moderations":
+            return clients.openai.moderations.create(
+                model=clients.plain_model, input=call.marker, extra_body=_NO_CACHE
+            ).id
+
+
+def _attempt(clients: _Clients, call: _Call) -> _Completed | _Failed:
+    try:
+        return _Completed(call, _invoke(clients, call))
+    except (OpenAiApiError, AnthropicApiError, httpx.HTTPError) as error:
+        return _Failed(call, f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:200]}")
+
+
+def _every_worker_serves_every_kind(gateway: Gateway, deployments: tuple[str, str]) -> bool:
+    calls: Final = _burst_calls(_ALL_KINDS, 2)
+    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(calls)) as pool:
+        futures: Final = _submit(pool, _clients(gateway, deployments), calls)
+        outcomes: Final = tuple(future.result(timeout=60) for future in futures)
+    return all(isinstance(outcome, _Completed) for outcome in outcomes)
+
+
+def _burst_calls(kinds: tuple[_Kind, ...], per_kind: int) -> tuple[_Call, ...]:
+    return tuple(_Call(kind, f"burst-{kind}-{uuid.uuid4().hex}") for kind, _ in product(kinds, range(per_kind)))
+
+
+def _submit(
+    pool: ThreadPoolExecutor, clients: _Clients, calls: tuple[_Call, ...]
+) -> tuple[Future[_Completed | _Failed], ...]:
+    return tuple(pool.submit(_attempt, clients, call) for call in calls)
+
+
+def _done_count(futures: tuple[Future[_Completed | _Failed], ...]) -> int:
+    return sum(future.done() for future in futures)
+
+
+def _liveliness(gateway: Gateway) -> int:
+    return gateway.client.get("/health/liveliness").status_code
+
+
+def _spend_rows(request_id: str) -> tuple[Mapping[str, JsonValue], ...]:
+    return tuple(read_rows(_SPEND_QUERY, (request_id,)))
+
+
+def _marker_counts(items: tuple[Mapping[str, JsonValue], ...], markers: tuple[str, ...]) -> tuple[int, ...]:
+    bodies: Final = tuple(json.dumps(item.get("body")) for item in items)
+    return tuple(sum(marker in body for body in bodies) for marker in markers)
+
+
+def _landed_once(response_ids: tuple[str, ...]) -> tuple[tuple[Mapping[str, JsonValue], ...], ...]:
+    rows: Final = tuple(
+        eventually(partial(_spend_rows, response_id), lambda values: len(values) == 1, seconds=90)
+        for response_id in response_ids
+    )
+    assert all(found[0]["request_id"] == response_id for found, response_id in zip(rows, response_ids)), rows
+    return rows
+

+def _is_worker(child: psutil.Process) -> bool:
+    try:
+        return "spawn_main" in " ".join(child.cmdline())
+    except psutil.Error:
+        return False
+
+
+def _worker_alive(worker: psutil.Process) -> bool:
+    try:
+        return worker.is_running() and worker.status() != psutil.STATUS_ZOMBIE
+    except psutil.NoSuchProcess:
+        return False
+
+
+def _alive_workers(process: subprocess.Popen[bytes]) -> tuple[psutil.Process, ...]:
+    children: Final = tuple(child for child in psutil.Process(process.pid).children() if _is_worker(child))
+    return tuple(child for child in children if _worker_alive(child))
+
+
+def _process_tree(process: subprocess.Popen[bytes]) -> str:
+    root: Final = psutil.Process(process.pid)
+    return "\n".join(_process_line(member) for member in (root, *root.children(recursive=True)))
+
+
+def _process_line(member: psutil.Process) -> str:
+    try:
+        return f"{member.pid} {' '.join(member.cmdline())}"
+    except psutil.Error:
+        return f"{member.pid} <exited>"
+

+def _kind_counts(outcomes: tuple[_Completed | _Failed, ...]) -> str:
+    kinds: Final = tuple(outcome.call.kind for outcome in outcomes)
+    return str({kind: kinds.count(kind) for kind in _ALL_KINDS if kind in kinds})

+def test_c01_upstream_pause_mid_burst_keeps_liveliness_and_lands_every_id_once(

+def _png_chunk(kind: bytes, data: bytes) -> bytes:

+def binary_response_types(legacy_response: httpx.Response, sdk_response: SDKResponse) -> None:
+    legacy: Final = HttpxBinaryResponseContent(legacy_response)
+    native: Final = HttpxBinaryResponseContent(sdk_response)
+
+    assert_type(legacy.response, httpx.Response)
+    assert_type(native.response, SDKResponse)
+    assert_type(legacy.read(), bytes)
+    assert_type(native.read(), bytes)
+    assert_type(consume_binary_response(legacy), httpx.Response)
+
+    sdk_wrapper: Final[SDKBinaryResponse] = legacy
+    assert_type(sdk_wrapper.read(), bytes)

title: [Bug]: Gemini candidate with a finishReason but no content is dropped, so the reason never reaches the client

judge.reasoning: Both patches fix the root cause (the `continue` on content-less candidates in `_process_candidates`) and both pass all nine independent tests, so the decision rests on edge handling and risk. Patch A keeps the change tight: it adds the NO_IMAGE/IMAGE_* mappings, appends an empty assistant choice with `native_finish_reason` only for the content-less case, maps `content_filter` to Anthropic `refusal`, and derives Responses `incomplete_details` from the finish reason. It also guards `stop_details` so a refusal translated from a bare `content_filter` with no refusal text does not emit refusal stop_details (which the comment notes would be read as a safeguard refusal and trigger fallbacks); Patch B leaves `refusal_stop_details(None)` unguarded on that new path. A's tests exercise the streaming `/v1/messages` path end-to-end through `AnthropicStreamWrapper`, which B only covers at the chunk level. Patch B is well-crafted and has broader tests (core_helpers table, adapter unit tests, Responses precedence test, multi-candidate state isolation), and fixing the shared per-candidate state in the loop is a legitimate improvement. But B also changes every Gemini choice to carry `provider_specific_fields={'native_finish_reason': ...}`, changes `tools` initialisation from `[]` to `None`, rewrites the finish-reason key set via `get_args`, and adds three more unmapped reasons; these widen the blast radius of the fix into all Gemini responses without evidence from the full suite, which is where scope beyond the ask counts against it. A's streaming reliance on the existing `_apply_stream_candidates` fallback is slightly less uniform than B's single path, but it is correct and verified. On balance A resolves the issue as specified with the fewest behavioural changes and the more careful handling of the refusal edge, so A edges it.

issue_md:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

When Gemini answers with a candidate that has a `finishReason` but no `content`, the gateway drops the candidate. `gemini-2.5-flash-image` served with `modalities: ["image"]` and asked a text-only question is a deterministic way to get one: Gemini returns `finishReason: NO_IMAGE` and no parts. Since PR #40294 the gateway no longer answers HTTP 500 on that shape, but what it returns instead carries no trace of why the model produced nothing: `/v1/chat/completions` comes back with `"choices": []` and no `finish_reason`, `/v1/messages` comes back with `"content": []` and `"stop_reason": "end_turn"`, and `/v1/responses` comes back with an empty `output` and `"status": "completed"`. A client cannot tell a declined request from an empty answer, and the same drop hides `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL` and `OTHER`. A thinking model that spends its whole budget on thoughts (`finishReason: MAX_TOKENS`, no `content`) hits the same branch and arrives with nonzero `output_tokens`: that case is #36881, with fix PRs #36870, #38301 and #40252 open, so a fix here should build on one of those rather than duplicate it

Expected: the completion carries one choice with an empty assistant message and a `finish_reason` mapped from Gemini's `finishReason` (raw value kept in the provider-specific fields), `/v1/messages` maps it to the matching Anthropic `stop_reason`, and `/v1/responses` carries the matching `incomplete_details`. Which OpenAI and Anthropic values `NO_IMAGE` and the other non-`STOP` reasons map to is a decision for the fix PR to record with its alternatives. Gemini safety blocks are a different path and already come back as a `content_filter` choice

### User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer asking an image model a text-only question gets an empty 200 with no reason attached, so their app shows a blank answer and logs nothing to explain it
1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "gemini-2.5-flash-image"` and a text-only user message
2. They get HTTP 200 with `"choices": []` and `"completion_tokens": 0`, no `finish_reason` anywhere
3. They send the same question as POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages and get HTTP 200 with `"content": []` and `"stop_reason": "end_turn"`, which reads as a normal, complete answer
4. They send it as POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses and get HTTP 200 with `"output": []` and `"status": "completed"`

After a (hypothetical) fix: the same requests still return 200, and each one says why the model produced nothing
1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "gemini-2.5-flash-image"` and a text-only user message
2. They get HTTP 200 with one choice, an empty assistant message, a `finish_reason` mapped from `NO_IMAGE`, and the raw `NO_IMAGE` value in the provider-specific fields
3. POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages returns HTTP 200 with `"content": []` and the matching `stop_reason`
4. POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses returns HTTP 200 with the matching `incomplete_details` instead of a bare `completed`

### Proof the bug occurs

Config the proxy ran with (`GEMINI_API_KEY` and `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` set in the environment, Redis on 127.0.0.1:21556):

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gemini-2.5-flash-image
    litellm_params:
      model: gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-image
      api_key: os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY
      modalities: ["image"]
litellm_settings:
  cache: true
  cache_params:
    type: redis
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 21556
    ttl: 900
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
```
