+"""
+A Gemini candidate can carry a finishReason but no ``content`` (e.g.
+``gemini-2.5-flash-image`` with ``modalities: ["image"]`` asked a text-only
+question answers ``finishReason: NO_IMAGE`` with no parts). The candidate must
+still surface as a choice so the reason reaches /v1/chat/completions,
+/v1/messages and /v1/responses instead of an empty, "completed" answer.
+"""
+
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock
+
+import httpx
+import pytest
+
+from litellm.llms.anthropic.experimental_pass_through.adapters.streaming_iterator import (
+    AnthropicStreamWrapper,
+)
+from litellm.llms.anthropic.experimental_pass_through.adapters.transformation import (
+    LiteLLMAnthropicMessagesAdapter,
+)
+from litellm.llms.vertex_ai.gemini.vertex_and_google_ai_studio_gemini import (
+    ModelResponseIterator,
+    VertexGeminiConfig,
+)
+from litellm.responses.litellm_completion_transformation.transformation import (
+    LiteLLMCompletionResponsesConfig,
+)
+from litellm.types.utils import ModelResponse
+
+
+def _content_less_body(finish_reason: str, thoughts_token_count: int = 0) -> dict:
+    usage: dict = {"promptTokenCount": 19, "totalTokenCount": 19 + thoughts_token_count}
+    if thoughts_token_count:
+        usage["thoughtsTokenCount"] = thoughts_token_count
+    return {
+        "candidates": [{"finishReason": finish_reason, "index": 0}],
+        "usageMetadata": usage,
+        "modelVersion": "gemini-2.5-flash-image",
+        "responseId": "resp-content-less",
+    }
+
+
+def _completion(body: dict) -> ModelResponse:
+    return VertexGeminiConfig()._transform_google_generate_content_to_openai_model_response(
+        completion_response=body,
+        model_response=ModelResponse(),
+        model="gemini-2.5-flash-image",
+        logging_obj=MagicMock(),
+        raw_response=httpx.Response(200, headers={}),
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("gemini_finish_reason", "openai_finish_reason"),
+    [
+        ("NO_IMAGE", "content_filter"),
+        ("MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL", "stop"),
+        ("OTHER", "content_filter"),
+        ("MAX_TOKENS", "length"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_chat_completion_keeps_content_less_candidate(gemini_finish_reason, openai_finish_reason):
+    response = _completion(_content_less_body(gemini_finish_reason))
+
+    assert len(response.choices) == 1
+    choice = response.choices[0]
+    assert choice.finish_reason == openai_finish_reason
+    assert choice.message.role == "assistant"
+    assert choice.message.content is None
+    assert choice.message.tool_calls is None
+    assert choice.provider_specific_fields == {"native_finish_reason": gemini_finish_reason}
+
+
+def test_chat_completion_thinking_budget_exhausted_reports_length():
+    response = _completion(_content_less_body("MAX_TOKENS", thoughts_token_count=256))
+
+    assert len(response.choices) == 1
+    assert response.choices[0].finish_reason == "length"
+    assert response.usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens == 256
+
+
+def test_messages_no_image_maps_to_refusal_stop_reason():
+    anthropic_response = LiteLLMAnthropicMessagesAdapter().translate_openai_response_to_anthropic(
+        response=_completion(_content_less_body("NO_IMAGE"))
+    )
+
+    assert anthropic_response["content"] == []
+    assert anthropic_response["stop_reason"] == "refusal"
+    # No refusal text came back, so this stays a plain refusal: stop_details
+    # would otherwise be read as a safeguard refusal and trigger fallbacks.
+    assert anthropic_response["stop_details"] is None
+
+
+def test_messages_max_tokens_maps_to_max_tokens_stop_reason():
+    anthropic_response = LiteLLMAnthropicMessagesAdapter().translate_openai_response_to_anthropic(
+        response=_completion(_content_less_body("MAX_TOKENS", thoughts_token_count=256))
+    )
+
+    assert anthropic_response["content"] == []
+    assert anthropic_response["stop_reason"] == "max_tokens"
+
+
+def test_messages_stream_no_image_maps_to_refusal_stop_reason():
+    iterator = ModelResponseIterator(streaming_response=iter([]), sync_stream=True, logging_obj=MagicMock())
+    chunk = iterator.chunk_parser(_content_less_body("NO_IMAGE"))
+    assert chunk.choices[0].finish_reason == "content_filter"
+
+    events = list(AnthropicStreamWrapper(completion_stream=iter([chunk]), model="gemini-2.5-flash-image"))
+
+    message_deltas = [e for e in events if e.get("type") == "message_delta"]
+    assert message_deltas, f"no message_delta emitted: {events}"
+    assert message_deltas[-1]["delta"]["stop_reason"] == "refusal"
+    assert "stop_details" not in message_deltas[-1]["delta"]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("gemini_finish_reason", "incomplete_reason"),
+    [("NO_IMAGE", "content_filter"), ("MAX_TOKENS", "max_output_tokens")],
+)
+def test_responses_reports_incomplete_details(gemini_finish_reason, incomplete_reason):
+    responses_response = LiteLLMCompletionResponsesConfig.transform_chat_completion_response_to_responses_api_response(
+        request_input="What is 2+2?",
+        responses_api_request={},
+        chat_completion_response=_completion(_content_less_body(gemini_finish_reason)),
+    )
+
+    assert responses_response.status == "incomplete"
+    assert responses_response.incomplete_details is not None
+    assert responses_response.incomplete_details.reason == incomplete_reason
+
+
+def test_responses_completed_answer_has_no_incomplete_details():
+    body = {
+        "candidates": [
+            {"content": {"role": "model", "parts": [{"text": "4"}]}, "finishReason": "STOP", "index": 0}
+        ],
+        "usageMetadata": {"promptTokenCount": 19, "candidatesTokenCount": 1, "totalTokenCount": 20},
+    }
+    responses_response = LiteLLMCompletionResponsesConfig.transform_chat_completion_response_to_responses_api_response(
+        request_input="What is 2+2?",
+        responses_api_request={},
+        chat_completion_response=_completion(body),
+    )
+
+    assert responses_response.status == "completed"
+    assert responses_response.incomplete_details is None

title: [Bug]: Completed /v1/responses requests retain max_parallel_requests slots during deferred logging

judge.reasoning: Both patches fix the root cause the same way: they release the stashed max_parallel_requests acquisition in async_post_call_success_hook, which the proxy awaits before returning a non-streaming response, and both guard against the deferred async_log_success_event releasing the same slot a second time. The independent tests pass on both. The difference is in how the double-release is prevented and in scope. Patch A detaches the acquisition from the stash before the first await, so under asyncio's single-threaded model the post-call hook and the deferred callback cannot both see a live slot; it needs no new state and touches only the two relevant sites. Patch B introduces an asyncio.Lock field on the per-request RequestRateLimiterStash dataclass and reroutes six release sites (pre-call rejections, failure event, disconnect, post-call failure) through the new locked helper. That refactor is consistent but goes well beyond the issue's ask and adds a synchronization primitive to a dataclass that is created per request, which is extra surface for little gain given the lockless pattern suffices. On tests, Patch A's first test runs the real ProxyLogging callback ordering with a slow logger ahead of the limiter, verifies the slot is free while logging is blocked, admits a follow-up request in a separate request context, and then verifies the late success event does not free the follow-up's slot; its second test forces a genuine interleave of the two releasers. Patch B's tests cover the same ground reasonably (including a Redis-failure concurrent release) but with more reliance on internal attributes like parallel_release_script. Patch A also documents why the post-call hook now owns the release. Patch B's one advantage is that keeping parallel_slot set until the release succeeds preserves retry-on-failure, but the release path already has an in-memory fallback, so this is marginal. A's narrower, lockless fix with strong tests is the better change.

issue_md:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

A completed non-streaming `/v1/responses` request can continue occupying its `max_parallel_requests` slot until asynchronous success logging finishes. With a virtual key limited to one parallel request, the first request returns `200`, but an identical request sent immediately afterward can incorrectly receive `429`. The next request succeeds once success logging completes.

The slot should be released before the completed response is returned to the caller. Slow logging integrations should not extend the request's concurrency lifetime.

This is related to #27955, but differs from the persistent slot leaks reported there: in this case the slot is eventually released, just too late. A proposed fix is in #40843.

### User Flow

Before a fix: a developer using the Responses API receives a false rate-limit response after the previous request has already completed.

1. The proxy administrator creates a virtual key with `max_parallel_requests: 1`.
2. The developer sends a non-streaming `POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses` request.
3. The completed request returns `200`.
4. The developer immediately sends the same request again and receives `429`.
5. After success logging finishes, the developer retries and receives `200`.

After a fix: the completed request releases its slot before returning, so the next request is admitted immediately.

1. The proxy administrator creates a virtual key with `max_parallel_requests: 1`.
2. The developer sends the same non-streaming `POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses` request.
3. The completed request returns `200`.
4. The developer immediately sends the same request again and also receives `200`.
5. Later requests continue receiving `200` after success logging finishes.

### Proof the bug occurs

The issue was reproduced against a real OpenAI-compatible Responses deployment with a local LiteLLM proxy, a virtual key limited to one parallel request, and a custom success logger that takes three seconds to complete. Secrets and provider-specific endpoint values are represented by environment variables below.

`slow_callback.py`:

```python
import asyncio

from litellm.integrations.custom_logger import CustomLogger


class SlowSuccessLogger(CustomLogger):
    async def async_log_success_event(
        self, kwargs, response_obj, start_time, end_time
    ) -> None:
        await asyncio.sleep(3)


slow_success_logger = SlowSuccessLogger()
```

Relevant `config.yaml`:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: responses-test
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/<model-name>
      api_base: os.environ/OPENAI_API_BASE
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY

litellm_settings:
  callbacks: slow_callback.slow_success_logger

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
```

Version tested before the fix:

```text
litellm_internal_staging at f90b5cad8a973eb8ddd94b3c8381c4ed83bba9f2
```

The same non-streaming request was sent three times: once initially, once immediately after the first response, and once after the three-second logging delay.

```text
first=200
immediate_next=429
after_logging=200
```

With the proposed fix from #40843 applied:

```text
first=200
```

title: [Bug]: thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01 beta header is stripped on /v1/messages, so thinking.block_binding 400s on Bedrock/Vertex

judge.reasoning:
Both patches fix the root cause identically for the providers the issue names: they register `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` in `anthropic_beta_headers_config.json` so `filter_and_transform_beta_headers` stops dropping it for anthropic, bedrock (invoke), and vertex_ai. The independent tests confirm both pass all five scenarios (Vertex, Bedrock invoke body `anthropic_beta`, first-party header, comma-separated list, Router with the issue's deployment config). The config edits are identical for the first five provider blocks; they differ only in the sixth block, where A forwards the header and B nulls it. That block is not a provider the issue names, so it does not decide the comparison.

B goes further in ways that matter for the same feature: (1) `AnthropicModelInfo` rewrites legacy `thinking: {type: enabled}` to `{type: adaptive}` for Fable 5.1 and previously discarded every other key, which would silently drop `block_binding` even once the header is forwarded; B carries `block_binding` through that rewrite, a low-risk two-line change directly tied to the issue's feature. (2) B adds `block_binding` to `AnthropicThinkingParam` and registers the beta in the `ANTHROPIC_BETA_HEADER_VALUES` enum, matching the convention visible in the surrounding code where each beta header has an enum member. 

On tests, A adds one parametrized unit test on the filter function, which does fail-before/pass-after but only exercises the allowlist lookup. B adds the same filter test plus end-to-end tests through `litellm.anthropic_messages` for anthropic, vertex_ai, and bedrock invoke that capture the outgoing request and assert both the beta (header or `anthropic_beta` body array) and `block_binding` survive, plus a regression test for the enabled→adaptive rewrite. These mirror the issue's reproduction far more faithfully and would catch regressions in the transformation layers, not just the JSON lookup.

A's broader coverage of a sixth provider and its `databricks` test parameter are a small point in its favor, but the issue does not ask for it and nothing in front of me confirms that block is databricks. Weighing correctness breadth within the feature, test strength, and consistency with codebase conventions, B is the better fix.

issue_md:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and this is not a duplicate (no hits for `thinking-binding-controls` or `block_binding`).

### What happened?

Anthropic's preserved-thinking controls for Claude Fable 5.1 (`thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior`, https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/preserved-thinking) are only accepted alongside the beta header `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01`.

When a client sends both through the proxy to a `bedrock/` or `vertex_ai/` Claude deployment on `/v1/messages`, the proxy forwards the `block_binding` body field untouched but strips the beta header, because the header has no entry in `anthropic_beta_headers_config.json` (bundled at v1.101.0-rc.1, and not on `main` as of `03a4c806c4` either). The provider then rejects the request with:

```
thinking.adaptive.block_binding: Extra inputs are not permitted
```

Consequences:

- Nobody behind a LiteLLM gateway can opt into preserved-thinking enforcement on Bedrock/Vertex, which Anthropic's docs tell integrators to do now to test their append-only behaviour before later models enforce it for everyone.
- Accounts created on or after 2026-08-31 are enforced by default on Fable 5.1; the SDKs send `block_binding` for them, so this is a hard 400 for those users rather than an opt-in inconvenience.

The same request sent directly to the provider (header + `block_binding`) succeeds and returns `input_transformations: []`.

### User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer testing their integration against preserved thinking gets a 400 from every Claude Fable 5.1 deployment behind the gateway.

1. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages` with header `anthropic-beta: thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` and body `"model": "claude-fable-5-1", "thinking": {"type": "adaptive", "block_binding": {"prefix_mismatch_behavior": "drop_block"}}, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "..."}]`
2. They get HTTP 400 `invalid_request_error`: `Vertex_aiException BadRequestError - thinking.adaptive.block_binding: Extra inputs are not permitted`, followed by the configured Bedrock fallback failing the same way (`BedrockException - {"message":"thinking.adaptive.block_binding: Extra inputs are not permitted"}`)
3. They remove the `block_binding` field: the request succeeds, but now they cannot see `input_transformations` or make the API enforce the prefix check, so they cannot tell whether their integration is affected

After a (hypothetical) fix: the same request goes through and the API reports what it dropped.

1. They send the same `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages` with the same header and body
2. They get HTTP 200 with the usual `content` array plus a top-level `input_transformations: []`
3. On a later turn where they edited an earlier message, `input_transformations` lists the dropped thinking blocks with `reason: "prefix_binding_mismatch"` (or, with `"error"`, the 400 Anthropic documents naming what changed)

### Proof the bug occurs

Config / setup the proxy ran with (our staging gateway, `litellm/litellm-database:v1.101.0-rc.1`, Vertex primary with Bedrock fallback; irrelevant deployments omitted):

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: claude-fable-5-1
    litellm_params:
      model: vertex_ai/claude-fable-5-1
      additional_drop_params: ["temperature"]
  - model_name: bedrock-claude-fable-5-1
    litellm_params:
      model: bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1
      aws_region_name: us-east-1
      thinking: {"type": "adaptive"}
litellm_settings:
  num_retries: 3
  drop_params: true
  fallbacks: [{"claude-fable-5-1": ["bedrock-claude-fable-5-1"]}]
  vertex_location: "global"
```

Env: `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` for Vertex, IRSA for Bedrock, no `LITELLM_LOCAL_ANTHROPIC_BETA_HEADERS`.

Version: `v1.101.0-rc.1` (image `litellm/litellm-database:v1.101.0-rc.1`).

Command (a 3-turn probe; turn 1 is enough to show it):

```
curl -sS https://<gateway>/v1/messages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <virtual key>" \
  -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
  -H "anthropic-beta: thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","max_tokens":4000,"output_config":{"effort":"high"},
       "thinking":{"type":"adaptive","block_binding":{"prefix_mismatch_behavior":"drop_block"}},
       "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Think carefully before answering. How many positive integers below 5000 have exactly 12 positive divisors? Reply with the number only."}]}'
```

Output (HTTP 400, `x-litellm-call-id: eb073562-5aa2-40f5-92f5-612477a7619c`):

```
{"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"litellm.BadRequestError: Vertex_aiException BadRequestError - {\"type\":\"error\",\"error\":{\"type\":\"invalid_request_error\",\"message\":\"thinking.adaptive.block_binding: Extra inputs are not permitted\"},\"request_id\":\"req_vrtx_011Cf4R9GhDLYQ5oqHS46VnE\"}. Received Model Group=claude-fable-5-1\nAvailable Model Group Fallbacks=['bedrock-claude-fable-5-1']\nError doing the fallback: litellm.BadRequestError: BedrockException - {\"message\":\"thinking.adaptive.block_binding: Extra inputs are not permitted\"} ..."}}
```

Same request against `bedrock-claude-fable-5-1` directly (`x-litellm-call-id: e0ddc96d-a555-4c57-84db-9266ab6adf15`): HTTP 400, `BedrockException - {"message":"thinking.adaptive.block_binding: Extra inputs are not permitted"}`.

Same request body without the beta header and without `block_binding`: HTTP 200 on all three turns, each response carries a `thinking` block with a `signature` and no `input_transformations` field (expected for an account created before 2026-08-31 with no opt-in).

After registering the header (branch `fix/anthropic-thinking-binding-beta-header`), the identical request to the same two deployments returns HTTP 200 and the response carries `input_transformations: []` — the field only exists when the header reached the provider — on both `bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1` and `vertex_ai/claude-fable-5-1`.

Where the header goes: `filter_and_transform_beta_headers` drops any value not present in the provider's mapping in `anthropic_beta_headers_config.json`; `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` has no entry for any provider. Confirmed on a local `litellm --config` proxy against a recording upstream: the outgoing Bedrock invoke body has `block_binding` but no `anthropic_beta`, and the outgoing first-party request has no `anthropic-beta` header.

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.101.0-rc.1

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_

+"""
+The ``thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01`` beta gates
+``thinking.block_binding`` (preserved-thinking controls). The beta allowlist
+used to have no entry for it, so /v1/messages forwarded ``block_binding`` but
+stripped the beta, and Bedrock / Vertex / Anthropic 400'd with
+``thinking.adaptive.block_binding: Extra inputs are not permitted``.
+"""
+
+import json
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import httpx
+import pytest
+
+import litellm
+from litellm import anthropic_beta_headers_manager
+from litellm.anthropic_beta_headers_manager import filter_and_transform_beta_headers
+
+THINKING_BINDING_BETA = "thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01"
+THINKING = {"type": "adaptive", "block_binding": {"prefix_mismatch_behavior": "drop_block"}}
+
+_ANTHROPIC_RESPONSE = {
+    "id": "msg_test",
+    "type": "message",
+    "role": "assistant",
+    "model": "claude-fable-5-1",
+    "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "ok"}],
+    "stop_reason": "end_turn",
+    "stop_sequence": None,
+    "usage": {"input_tokens": 1, "output_tokens": 1},
+    "input_transformations": [],
+}
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def bundled_beta_allowlist(monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setenv("LITELLM_LOCAL_ANTHROPIC_BETA_HEADERS", "True")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(anthropic_beta_headers_manager, "_BETA_HEADERS_CONFIG", None)
+    yield
+    monkeypatch.setattr(anthropic_beta_headers_manager, "_BETA_HEADERS_CONFIG", None)
+
+
+def _betas_from_header(headers):
+    return {b.strip() for b in (headers.get("anthropic-beta") or "").split(",") if b.strip()}
+
+
+async def _send_messages_request(model, **kwargs):
+    captured = []
+
+    async def mock_post(self, url, data=None, headers=None, **kwargs):
+        body = kwargs.get("json")
+        if body is None:
+            body = data if isinstance(data, dict) else json.loads(data)
+        captured.append({"url": str(url), "headers": dict(headers or {}), "body": body})
+        return httpx.Response(
+            status_code=200,
+            content=json.dumps(_ANTHROPIC_RESPONSE).encode(),
+            headers={"content-type": "application/json"},
+            request=httpx.Request("POST", str(url)),
+        )
+
+    try:
+        with patch("litellm.llms.custom_httpx.http_handler.AsyncHTTPHandler.post", new=mock_post):
+            response = await litellm.anthropic_messages(
+                model=model,
+                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "How many divisors?"}],
+                max_tokens=4000,
+                thinking=kwargs.pop("thinking", THINKING),
+                extra_headers={"anthropic-beta": THINKING_BINDING_BETA},
+                **kwargs,
+            )
+    finally:
+        await litellm.close_litellm_async_clients()
+
+    assert len(captured) == 1
+    return response, captured[0]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_anthropic_messages_forwards_thinking_binding_beta_to_anthropic():
+    response, request = await _send_messages_request(
+        model="anthropic/claude-fable-5-1",
+        api_key="sk-ant-test",
+    )
+
+    assert THINKING_BINDING_BETA in _betas_from_header(request["headers"])
+    assert request["body"]["thinking"]["block_binding"] == THINKING["block_binding"]
+    assert response["content"][0]["text"] == "ok"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_anthropic_messages_forwards_thinking_binding_beta_to_vertex_ai():
+    from litellm.llms.vertex_ai.vertex_llm_base import VertexBase
+
+    with patch.object(VertexBase, "_ensure_access_token", return_value=("ya29.token", "test-project")):
+        response, request = await _send_messages_request(
+            model="vertex_ai/claude-fable-5-1",
+            vertex_project="test-project",
+            vertex_location="global",
+        )
+
+    assert THINKING_BINDING_BETA in _betas_from_header(request["headers"])
+    assert request["body"]["thinking"]["block_binding"] == THINKING["block_binding"]
+    assert response["content"][0]["text"] == "ok"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_anthropic_messages_forwards_thinking_binding_beta_to_bedrock_invoke():
+    response, request = await _send_messages_request(
+        model="bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1",
+        aws_access_key_id="AKIAFAKE",
+        aws_secret_access_key="fake-secret",
+        aws_region_name="us-east-1",
+    )
+
+    assert THINKING_BINDING_BETA in request["body"].get("anthropic_beta", [])
+    assert request["body"]["thinking"]["block_binding"] == THINKING["block_binding"]
+    assert response["content"][0]["text"] == "ok"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "model, provider_kwargs",
+    [
+        ("anthropic/claude-fable-5-1", {"api_key": "sk-ant-test"}),
+        (
+            "bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1",
+            {"aws_access_key_id": "AKIAFAKE", "aws_secret_access_key": "fake-secret", "aws_region_name": "us-east-1"},
+        ),
+    ],
+)
+async def test_legacy_enabled_thinking_keeps_block_binding_on_adaptive_model(model, provider_kwargs):
+    """Legacy ``type: enabled`` is rewritten to adaptive for Fable 5.1; the
+    rewrite must not drop ``block_binding``."""
+    _, request = await _send_messages_request(
+        model=model,
+        thinking={"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 2048, "block_binding": THINKING["block_binding"]},
+        **provider_kwargs,
+    )
+
+    assert request["body"]["thinking"] == {"type": "adaptive", "block_binding": THINKING["block_binding"]}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("provider", ["anthropic", "bedrock", "bedrock_converse", "vertex_ai"])
+def test_thinking_binding_beta_survives_provider_allowlist(provider):
+    assert filter_and_transform_beta_headers([THINKING_BINDING_BETA], provider=provider) == [THINKING_BINDING_BETA]

judge.reasoning: Patch B resolves the full ask: all 14 chatgpt/* rows gain supports_reasoning and matching effort flags in both the main and backup cost maps, including the two twinless rows (gpt-5.3-codex-spark, gpt-5.3-instant), and the gpt-5.6-{sol,terra,luna} rows get supports_max_reasoning_effort as the issue's secondary request. It updates the explanatory comment in reasoning_effort_capability.py to reflect the new max-flag carriers and adds focused tests (twin-parity across both files, every chatgpt row flagged, resolver returns the max tier, get_model_info end-to-end for chatgpt/gpt-5.6-sol). Independent tests pass across the board for B. Patch A leaves gpt-5.3-codex-spark and gpt-5.3-instant unannotated and never adds supports_max_reasoning_effort, so it fails 15 of the independent tests. It also bundles a large amount of unrelated churn with real risk: repricing azure/gpt-5.6 and its regional variants, changing bedrock claude-mythos pricing, adding anthropic batch rates, changing bing grounding cost (and editing an existing test assertion to match), adding many new model rows, Rust struct fields, Python type fields, schema entries and UI typings. None of that relates to the issue, and the pricing edits in particular could alter billing. A's one advantage is carrying default_reasoning_effort for gpt-5.4/gpt-5.2 from the openai twins, which B omits, but that is a minor gap not called out in the issue and does not offset the missed rows, missing max flag, and unrelated risky changes.

issue_md:
## What happened

Every model entry under the `chatgpt/` provider prefix is missing its reasoning-capability annotations, even though the identical underlying models are fully annotated under the `openai/` and `azure/` prefixes.

All 14 `chatgpt/*` entries in `model_prices_and_context_window.json` (main) have **zero** reasoning keys — no `supports_reasoning`, no `supports_*_reasoning_effort`:

```
$ jq -r '[to_entries[]|select(.key|startswith("chatgpt/"))] |
    "total: \(length)",
    "with supports_reasoning: \([.[]|select(.value.supports_reasoning != null)]|length)",
    "with any effort flag: \([.[]|select(.value|to_entries|any(.key|test("reasoning_effort")))]|length)"' \
  model_prices_and_context_window.json
total: 14
with supports_reasoning: 0
with any effort flag: 0
```

Affected keys:

```
chatgpt/gpt-5.1-codex-max     chatgpt/gpt-5.3-codex-spark   chatgpt/gpt-5.6-luna
chatgpt/gpt-5.1-codex-mini    chatgpt/gpt-5.3-instant       chatgpt/gpt-5.6-sol
chatgpt/gpt-5.2               chatgpt/gpt-5.4               chatgpt/gpt-5.6-terra
chatgpt/gpt-5.2-codex         chatgpt/gpt-5.4-pro
chatgpt/gpt-5.3-chat-latest   chatgpt/gpt-5.5
chatgpt/gpt-5.3-codex
```

## The inconsistency

Same model, three prefixes, two different answers:

```jsonc
// chatgpt/gpt-5.6-sol — no reasoning keys at all
{
  "litellm_provider": "chatgpt",
  "source": "https://platform.openai.com/docs/models/gpt-5.6-sol",
  "max_input_tokens": 1050000,
  "max_output_tokens": 128000,
  "mode": "responses",
  "supported_endpoints": ["/v1/chat/completions", "/v1/responses"],
  "supports_function_calling": true,
  "supports_vision": true
}

// gpt-5.6-sol (litellm_provider: openai) — annotated
{
  "mode": "chat",
  "supports_reasoning": true,
  "supports_none_reasoning_effort": true,
  "supports_minimal_reasoning_effort": false,
  "supports_xhigh_reasoning_effort": true
}

// azure/gpt-5.6-sol — annotated
{
  "mode": "chat",
  "supports_reasoning": true,
  "supports_none_reasoning_effort": true,
  "supports_minimal_reasoning_effort": false,
  "supports_xhigh_reasoning_effort": true
}
```

`chatgpt/gpt-5.6-sol` is a reasoning model — it accepts `reasoning_effort`, and `/model/info` lists it in `supported_openai_params`. It just never says so in the cost map.

## Impact

Any consumer that reads capabilities from `/model/info` sees a reasoning model advertising no reasoning support. Concretely, for a route declared as:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: high
    litellm_params:
      model: chatgpt/gpt-5.6-sol
```

`/model/info` returns `supports_reasoning: null` and every `supports_*_reasoning_effort: null`. Downstream clients that gate their thinking/effort UI on these flags disable reasoning controls entirely, or fall back to a hardcoded subset. The only workaround is to hand-write `model_info` per route:

```yaml
    model_info:
      supports_reasoning: true
      supports_none_reasoning_effort: true
      supports_minimal_reasoning_effort: false
      supports_xhigh_reasoning_effort: true
      supports_max_reasoning_effort: true
```

which duplicates data LiteLLM already carries for the `openai/` and `azure/` spellings of the same model.

## Secondary: `supports_max_reasoning_effort` missing on all gpt-5.6 variants

Separate from the `chatgpt/` gap — no gpt-5.6 entry under **any** prefix declares `supports_max_reasoning_effort`, though the models do accept `effort: "max"`. models.dev reports for `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`:

```json
"reasoning_options": [
  { "type": "effort", "values": ["none", "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"] }
]
```

Verified end-to-end against a live proxy — `reasoning_effort: "max"` against a `chatgpt/gpt-5.6-sol` route is accepted and returns `reasoning_tokens > 0`.

For reference, the flag is well-established in the map (`supports_max_reasoning_effort` appears on 32 entries, `supports_xhigh_reasoning_effort` on 63), so this is a per-model omission rather than a schema question.

## Suggested fix

Propagate the reasoning annotations from the `openai/` entries to their `chatgpt/` counterparts, and add `supports_max_reasoning_effort: true` to the gpt-5.6 family. For `chatgpt/gpt-5.6-{sol,terra,luna}`:

```jsonc
{
  "supports_reasoning": true,
  "supports_none_reasoning_effort": true,
  "supports_minimal_reasoning_effort": false,
  "supports_xhigh_reasoning_effort": true,
  "supports_max_reasoning_effort": true
}
```

(`medium`/`high` intentionally omitted — consistent with the rest of the map, which never declares them and treats them as the implicit baseline.)

Happy to open a PR for the data change if that's the preferred route.

## Environment

- LiteLLM 1.86.0, self-hosted proxy, ChatGPT/Codex OAuth backend (`chatgpt` provider, `mode: responses`)
- Cost map fetched live from `main` (4030 entries) rather than the bundled backup (2716 entries) — the gap is present in both

+        if isinstance(entry, dict) and entry.get("litellm_provider") == "chatgpt"
+        for twin in [rows.get(name.removeprefix("chatgpt/"))]
+        if isinstance(twin, dict) and twin.get("litellm_provider") == "openai"
+        for flag, value in twin.items()
+        if REASONING_FLAG.match(flag) and entry.get(flag) != value
+    ]
+    assert drifted == [], "\n".join(drifted)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", (PRICES_PATH, BACKUP_PRICES_PATH), ids=("main", "backup"))
+def test_every_chatgpt_row_is_flagged_as_reasoning(path: Path):
+    """Every model the ChatGPT backend serves is a gpt-5+ reasoning model, including the ones
+    with no openai twin to inherit from."""
+    rows: Final = json.loads(path.read_text())
+    unflagged: Final = [
+        name
+        for name, entry in rows.items()
+        if isinstance(entry, dict)
+        and entry.get("litellm_provider") == "chatgpt"
+        and entry.get("supports_reasoning") is not True
+    ]
+    assert unflagged == []
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", ("chatgpt/gpt-5.6-sol", "chatgpt/gpt-5.6-terra", "chatgpt/gpt-5.6-luna"))
+def test_chatgpt_gpt_5_6_rows_advertise_max(prices: dict, name: str):
+    """The ChatGPT backend serves gpt-5.6 over the Responses API only, and that surface accepts
+    reasoning_effort='max' (a chatgpt/gpt-5.6-sol route answers it with reasoning tokens). The bare
+    openai rows stay at xhigh because their /v1/chat/completions refuses max. max is opt-in for the
+    resolver, so a row without the flag drops it from every group it belongs to."""
+    assert resolve_supported_reasoning_efforts(prices[name], deployment_is_mapped=True) == (
+        "none",
+        "low",
+        "medium",
+        "high",
+        "xhigh",
+        "max",
+    )
+
+
+def test_chatgpt_gpt_5_6_model_info_reports_reasoning_support():
+    """What /model/info serves for a `model: chatgpt/gpt-5.6-sol` route."""
+    info: Final = litellm.get_model_info(model="gpt-5.6-sol", custom_llm_provider="chatgpt")
+    assert (
+        info["key"],
+        info["supports_reasoning"],
+        info["supports_none_reasoning_effort"],
+        info["supports_minimal_reasoning_effort"],
+        info["supports_xhigh_reasoning_effort"],
+        info["supports_max_reasoning_effort"],
+    ) == ("chatgpt/gpt-5.6-sol", True, True, False, True, True)
+
+

+    os.environ["LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP"] = "True"
+    litellm.model_cost = litellm.get_model_cost_map(url="")

+    prefixes = ("us.", "eu.", "apac.", "us-gov.", "au.", "global.")
+    checked = 0
+
+    for k, v in litellm.model_cost.items():
+        if not str(v.get("litellm_provider", "")).startswith("bedrock"):
+            continue
+        base_model_key = next(

+                    base.get(cost_key) or 0

title: [Bug]: LiteLLM Proxy 1.100.0 serializes image-edit uploads as strings for OpenAI GPT Image models

judge.reasoning:
Both patches fix the actual defect in the same way: the raw `image[]` / `mask[]` form parts remain in the parsed body after FastAPI binds them to the `image_array`/`mask_array` parameters, so they are forwarded as extra provider params and stringified into text multipart fields. A pops them from `data`; B filters them out in a dict comprehension. Both pass all three independent tests that fail on base, so correctness on the reported scenario is equal.

The differences are in tests and extra hardening. Patch A's regression test is materially stronger: it drives the request through the proxy endpoint and then through `litellm.aimage_edit` with an httpx MockTransport, and asserts on the actual multipart body sent to OpenAI (image[] and mask parts are file parts with the original bytes, no `UploadFile`/`BytesIO` repr anywhere), parameterized over both `image[]` and `image` spellings. That directly mirrors the failure the issue reports at the wire level. Patch B's tests only inspect the kwargs captured at `route_request`; they do fail on base (since `image[]` would be present) and cover mask[] and the canonical fields, but stop short of the provider serialization that actually produced the OpenAI error.

Patch A also makes `_form_field_value` raise a TypeError for bytes/file-like values instead of silently shipping a repr string. This is scope beyond the ask and carries a small risk of turning a previously-garbage request into an exception for any other caller, but on base such a request was already broken, so failing loudly is a reasonable guard against recurrence and is covered by unit tests. Patch B, by contrast, includes unrelated formatting churn in existing tests (reflowing `monkeypatch.setattr` lines and function signatures), which is neutral-to-slightly-negative noise.

Craft is comparable: B's named constants and comprehension are tidy; A's comment explains why the pop is needed. On balance A wins on the stronger, end-to-end regression test that targets the exact symptom in the issue, with the hardening being acceptable and tested.

### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

Image edits through the LiteLLM Proxy fail in version 1.100.0 for OpenAI GPT Image models. The uploaded image file is being converted to a string representation of a Python `BytesIO` object (`"<_io.BytesIO object at 0x7f0d0bc73600>"`) before being sent to OpenAI.

OpenAI rejects this with:
```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Invalid type for 'image[0]': expected a file, but got a string instead.",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "param": "image[0]",
    "code": "invalid_type"
  }
}
```

The same request succeeds in LiteLLM version 1.95.0.

### User Flow

Before a fix: A user sends an image-edit request through LiteLLM Proxy 1.100.0 using a multipart/form-data request to POST /v1/images/edits with an uploaded image file and a prompt (e.g., "Make this image photorealistic"). LiteLLM receives the UploadFile correctly but serializes it to a string before forwarding to OpenAI. OpenAI rejects the request because it expects a file object, not a string representation.

1. User sends: `curl -X POST "http://localhost:4000/v1/images/edits" -F "model=openai/gpt-image-2" -F "prompt=Make this image photorealistic" -F "image[]=@./input.png;type=image/png"`
2. LiteLLM receives UploadFile with filename, size, and content-type headers
3. LiteLLM converts the UploadFile's BytesIO object to a string
4. LiteLLM forwards stringified image to OpenAI
5. OpenAI rejects with invalid_type error

After a fix: The same user flow succeeds. LiteLLM preserves the UploadFile/BytesIO object and forwards it to OpenAI as a multipart file, and OpenAI processes it successfully.

### Proof the bug occurs

Config / setup the proxy ran with:
Default LiteLLM Proxy setup with OpenAI API key configured

Version or commit:
1.100.0 (regression; works in 1.95.0)

Commands and their full output:
```bash
curl -X POST "http://localhost:4000/v1/images/edits" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_API_KEY" \
  -F "model=openai/gpt-image-2" \
  -F "prompt=Make this image photorealistic" \
  -F "image[]=@./input.png;type=image/png"
```

LiteLLM request logging shows:
- Receives: `image[]: UploadFile(filename='...png', size=2014638, headers=Headers({'content-type': 'image/png', 'content-disposition': 'form-data; name="image[]"; filename="...png"'}))`
- Sends to OpenAI: `{"image": ["<_io.BytesIO object at 0x7f0d0bc73600>"], "model": "openai/gpt-image-2", "prompt": "..."}`

OpenAI error response:
```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Invalid type for 'image[0]': expected a file, but got a string instead.",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "param": "image[0]",
    "code": "invalid_type"
  }
}
```

Stack trace passes through: `litellm/proxy/image_endpoints/endpoints.py:313` and `litellm/images/main.py:1038`

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

1.100.0

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_

+    """(field name, is a file part, payload) for each part of a multipart body."""
+    boundary = content_type.split("boundary=")[1].encode()
+    parts = []
+    for part in body.split(b"--" + boundary):
+        if b'name="' not in part:
+            continue
+        headers, _, payload = part.partition(b"\r\n\r\n")
+        name = headers.split(b'name="')[1].split(b'"')[0].decode()
+        parts.append((name, b"filename=" in headers, payload.rstrip(b"\r\n-")))
+    return parts
+

title: [Bug]: Fix "vertex_ai/xai/grok-4.6" entry in "model_prices_and_context_window.json" — missing supports_prompt_caching

judge.reasoning: Neither diff shows a change to model_prices_and_context_window.json or the backup map, and the independent tests all pass on base, so the catalog data itself cannot distinguish the patches; the comparison comes down to the test changes. Patch A adds a parametrized test that drives the proxy's _enrich_model_info_with_litellm_data for every vertex_ai/xai/grok-* model in the issue's table and asserts provider, supports_prompt_caching, and the exact cache_read_input_token_cost from the table. That directly covers the GET /model/info deployment path the issue reports and pins the whole family, not just grok-4.6. Patch B only reworks existing tests: it swaps supports_prompt_caching() for get_model_info() in the sweep (lateral, since one wraps the other), adds cache-price truthiness checks and a catalog lookup for grok-4.6, and sprinkles `Final` annotations on local variables, which is unusual and adds no value. B's edits are modest polish with slight churn; A's addition is the more meaningful regression guard for the scenario described. Scope and risk are otherwise comparable, so A is the better patch.

### What happened?

https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.102.0-rc.1/model_prices_and_context_window.json#L48398-L48416

This entry has `cache_read_input_token_cost` (5e-07) and `cache_read_input_token_cost_above_200k_tokens` (1e-06) but no `supports_prompt_caching`, so `supports_prompt_caching()` returns false and `GET /v1/model/info` reports `"supports_prompt_caching": false` for a Vertex Grok 4.6 deployment.

The same model on the other providers does set it:

- `xai/grok-4.6` → `supports_prompt_caching: true` (L49979)
- `azure_ai/grok-4.6` → `supports_prompt_caching: true`

xAI prompt caching is provider-managed (automatic on a stable prefix), and the Vertex route does return `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` > 0 on follow-up turns, which is what the cache-read rate on this entry bills. title: [Bug]: Databricks service_tier is dropped in request translation, streaming, and pricing

judge.reasoning: Both patches add service_tier to the Databricks supported-params list, read the tier from responses_api_request in the Responses-to-Chat bridge, and stamp the provider-returned tier in DatabricksConfig.transform_response. Patch B stops there: it does nothing for streaming, so the issue's explicit 'tier on terminal usage-only chunk' case remains broken. The independent tests confirm this: B fails all three streaming tests (stream_chunk_builder aggregation and the logged complete streaming response with and without include_usage), while A passes every one of the ten tests. Patch A fixes the streaming gap at the point where CustomStreamWrapper handles the usage-only chunk, widens the existing _stamp_served_service_tier helper to accept any BaseModel, and also propagates the served tier into the Responses API response without manufacturing one from the request, matching the issue's expected behavior. A's added validation that rejects non-Databricks tiers like 'flex' unless drop_params is set goes somewhat beyond the ask, but it is small, consistent with litellm's UnsupportedParamsError convention, and low risk. A's tests are broader and exercise the real end-to-end paths (chunk_parser, CustomStreamWrapper, stream_chunk_builder, pricing with returned-default override); B's tests cover only params, non-stream parsing, and the request bridge. A fully covers the issue's four symptom rows and B covers only three, so A is the better fix.

issue_md:
## Summary

In LiteLLM 1.100.0, Databricks `service_tier="priority"` can be dropped during request translation and parameter filtering. Databricks cost calculation also ignores the resolved tier, so configured priority input/output/cache-read rates are not used. Returned tiers are lost in response conversion and streaming aggregation.

These defects need to be handled together: fixing pricing alone can apply requested priority rates even when Databricks reports `service_tier="default"` after fallback.

## Reproduction and environment

Reproduced with a clean installation of `litellm[proxy]==1.100.0` on Python 3.11 in an isolated virtual environment. The portable pytest file will be attached in a follow-up comment. It uses synthetic model prices and response objects; no API credentials, provider calls, proxy, or downstream repository files are required.

Save the attached file as `test_databricks_service_tier_upstream.py`, outside any existing checkout, and run:

```bash
python3 -m venv /tmp/databricks-tier-repro
/tmp/databricks-tier-repro/bin/pip install 'litellm[proxy]==1.100.0' pytest
LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True /tmp/databricks-tier-repro/bin/python -m pytest -q test_databricks_service_tier_upstream.py
```

Observed results: **6 failed, 7 passed**.

| Case | Expected | Actual on 1.100.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Priority pricing from explicit argument, request params, or response | $0.000568 | $0.000284 in all three cases |
| Responses-to-Chat request translation | `service_tier="priority"` preserved | Field absent (`KeyError`) |
| Databricks parameter mapping with `drop_params=True` | `service_tier="priority"` preserved | Field absent (`KeyError`) |
| Stream with tier on terminal usage-only chunk | Aggregated response has `service_tier="default"` | `None` |

The synthetic pricing case has 100 input tokens (20 cached) and 50 output tokens. Standard rates are $1/$4 per million input/output tokens and $0.20 per million cached input tokens; priority rates are twice those values.

Default pricing, legacy Databricks model resolution, and returned-default fallback controls pass on stock 1.100.0. The fallback controls pass because stock Databricks pricing always uses standard rates; they must continue to pass after priority pricing is enabled. All 13 tests pass with a local fix.

## Root cause

Source locations refer to LiteLLM 1.100.0:

- `litellm/llms/databricks/chat/transformation.py`, `DatabricksConfig.get_supported_openai_params` (~line 259): `service_tier` is absent from the supported parameter list.
- `litellm/responses/litellm_completion_transformation/transformation.py`, `transform_responses_api_request_to_chat_completion_request` (~line 340): reads `kwargs.get("service_tier")`, but the tier is in `responses_api_request`. Adding only the Databricks allowlist entry does not repair this earlier loss.
- `litellm/cost_calculator.py` (~line 623) and `litellm/llms/databricks/cost_calculator.py` (~line 34): the Databricks dispatch/helper do not pass `service_tier` through to `generic_cost_per_token`.
- `litellm/litellm_core_utils/streaming_chunk_builder_utils.py`: stream aggregation does not carry the returned tier, including when it arrives only on the final usage chunk. Databricks response parsing, stream-wrapper reconstruction, and Chat/Responses/Messages conversion also need to preserve it for end-to-end accounting.
- `completion_cost` currently gives a requested tier precedence over a returned tier. For Databricks, a concrete returned `default` tier should override requested priority.

Additional Router/HTTP-interception tests exposed a related Messages-stream accounting issue: `litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/adapters/streaming_iterator.py` calls `stream_chunk_builder` without its existing request logging object. Standalone cost calculation can then miss Router pricing and cache a zero cost. Passing the logging object preserves the configured pricing context. This path is covered by the broader local regression suite, not the 13-test portable file.

## Expected behavior

- Forward supported Databricks `default`/`priority` tiers through Chat, Responses, and Messages bridges, including streaming.
- Preserve provider-returned tiers through response parsing, adapters, stream reconstruction/aggregation, and accounting.
- Apply configured tier-specific input, output, and cache-read prices.
- Use a concrete returned Databricks tier over the requested tier; retain standard pricing and legacy model-name resolution.
- If the provider omits a returned tier, do not manufacture one. Requested-tier pricing is an estimate, not evidence of the tier delivered or invoiced.

Databricks documents priority fallback and model/region availability here: https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/machine-learning/foundation-model-apis/priority-mode

I searched open and closed issues for Databricks priority/service-tier symptoms and the affected function names and found no matching report. PR #35674 concerns cache pricing and does not address these tier-propagation gaps.

title: [Bug]: Vertex Grok (`vertex_ai/xai/grok-*`) is rejected on `/v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent` while `/v1/chat/completions` on the same deployment works

judge.reasoning: Both patches fix the root cause the issue names: the generateContent config selector now consults the same route determination chat routing uses (get_vertex_ai_model_route), so vertex_ai/xai/grok-* returns None and falls through to the completion adapter. The independent tests confirm both make all four failing Grok scenarios pass with no regressions to Gemini, Claude, or chat completions. Patch B is a tight, two-file change that does exactly what the issue's 'narrow fix' paragraph asks, plus focused tests: an end-to-end mocked agenerate_content and agenerate_content_stream for vertex_ai/xai/grok-4.6 asserting the upstream URL is the openapi chat/completions endpoint and the Gemini-shaped output joins to '144', and a parametrized config-selection test. Its one gap is not forwarding litellm_params (base_model), so a numeric tuned-Gemini endpoint would now take the adapter path instead of native generateContent; that still works functionally but is a small behavior shift. Patch A's core fix is arguably more principled (uses_vertex_gemini_api, forwards base_model, covers gemma/agent_engine), but it is buried in a very large, mostly unrelated change set: a rewrite of cost_per_token prefix stripping in cost_calculator.py, a rewrite of the Databricks SSE iterator, changed exception semantics in the GenAI adapter handler (no longer wraps in ValueError, marks logging complete), a finish-chunk-holding mechanism in the stream wrapper, new stream_options injection in proxy request processing, a VertexAITokenCounter early-return, and ~1,500 lines of integration tests that depend on infrastructure outside the issue. Several of these (cost calculation, error types, token counting) alter behavior for callers unrelated to Grok and carry real regression risk, and they obscure the actual fix. Under the stated weighting, B resolves the issue at its root with targeted, non-tautological tests and minimal risk, while A's extras count against it rather than for it.

### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

A proxy with a single Vertex Model Garden Grok deployment (`vertex_ai/xai/grok-4.6`) serves that model correctly on `/v1/chat/completions`, but the same `model_name` on the unified Gemini-style endpoint `POST /v1beta/models/grok-4.6:generateContent` fails.

On the same proxy and the same endpoint:

- `gemini-*` deployments succeed.
- Vertex Claude deployments succeed (they are translated to their own chat protocol).
- `vertex_ai/xai/grok-*` deployments fail.

**Expected:** `/v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent` should serve a Vertex `xai/grok-*` deployment the same way it already serves other non-Gemini Vertex publisher models (Claude, Mistral, gpt-oss, Qwen, MiniMax, Moonshot, Z.ai, Gemma MaaS) — by translating the request to that model's chat-completions protocol and returning a normal `candidates[...]` response — instead of treating Grok as a native Gemini model.

**Suspected cause (for maintainers):** two different checks decide how a Vertex model is served, and they disagree about the `xai/` publisher.

- `litellm/llms/vertex_ai/common_utils.py::get_vertex_ai_model_route()` has an explicit `model.startswith("xai/")` branch returning `MODEL_GARDEN`, so chat completions work.
- `litellm/utils.py::ProviderConfigManager.get_provider_google_genai_generate_content_config()` falls back to the `litellm.completion()` adapter only when `VertexAIPartnerModels.is_vertex_partner_model()` is true, and `PartnerModelPrefixes` has no `xai/` entry, so Grok is handed to `VertexAIGoogleGenAIConfig` (native Gemini) instead.

Note that simply adding `xai/` to `PartnerModelPrefixes` would regress chat completions: `is_vertex_partner_model()` is evaluated before the `xai/` Model Garden branch, and the partner handler raises `Unknown partner model` for `xai/`. The narrow fix is to make the `generateContent` handler selection use the same Model Garden determination that chat routing already uses.

### User Flow

**Before a (hypothetical) fix** — the flow breaks the first time the user sends a Grok request to the Gemini-style URL, even though every other model at that same URL works and Grok itself works at the OpenAI-style URL.

1. The user lists the gateway catalog with `GET http://localhost:4000/v1/models` and sees both `gemini-2.5-flash` and `grok-4.6` offered.
2. The user sends `POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions` with `{"model": "grok-4.6", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is 12*12? Reply with only the number."}]}` and gets `200` with `choices[0].message.content` = `144`.
3. The user points their Google GenAI SDK app at the gateway and sends `POST http://localhost:4000/v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-flash:generateContent` with `{"contents": [...]}` and gets `200` with `candidates[0].content.parts[0].text` = `144`.
4. The user sends the identical body to `POST http://localhost:4000/v1beta/models/claude-opus-4-5:generateContent` for their Vertex Claude deployment and gets `200` with the same `candidates[...]` shape, confirming the endpoint is not Gemini-only.
5. The user sends the identical body to `POST http://localhost:4000/v1beta/models/grok-4.6:generateContent` and instead of `200` gets an error naming the Gemini publisher path for a model that is not a Gemini publisher model.
6. The user retries streaming at `POST http://localhost:4000/v1beta/models/grok-4.6:streamGenerateContent` and gets the same failure, with no chunks.
7. The user has to keep a second client stack on the OpenAI-style route just for Grok, and cannot offer Grok to Google GenAI SDK / Gemini CLI users at all.

+    "choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {"role": "assistant", "content": "hello"}, "finish_reason": None}]

+_FINISH_CHUNK: Final = {"choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {}, "finish_reason": "stop"}]}
+_USAGE_CHUNK: Final = {"choices": [], "usage": _TEXT_USAGE}
+_TEXT_DELTA: Final = _text_frame(_DELTA_CHUNK)
+_TEXT_FINISH: Final = _text_frame(_FINISH_CHUNK)
+_TEXT_USAGE_FRAME: Final = _text_frame(_USAGE_CHUNK)
+_TEXT_DONE: Final = b"data: [DONE]\n\n"

+def _billed_text_frames(include_usage: bool) -> tuple[bytes, ...]:
+    response_id: Final = f"chatcmpl-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
+    chunks: Final = (_DELTA_CHUNK, _FINISH_CHUNK, *((_USAGE_CHUNK,) if include_usage else ()))
+    return (*(_text_frame(chunk, response_id) for chunk in chunks), _TEXT_DONE)
+

+def _gemini_frames(response_text: str) -> list[dict]:

+    assert all(part.startswith("data: ") for part in parts), response_text
+    return [json.loads(part.removeprefix("data: ")) for part in parts]
+

+def _stop_frames(frames: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
+    return [frame for frame in frames if any(c.get("finishReason") for c in frame.get("candidates", []))]

+    "model_garden_endpoint": Route("openai/1234567890123456789", "us-central1", adapter=True),
+    "gemma": Route(
+        "gemma/gemma-2-2b-it",
+        "us-central1",
+        adapter=True,
+        endpoint_path=f"/v1/projects/{_PROJECT}/locations/us-central1/endpoints/4242:predict",
+    ),
+    "gemini": Route("gemini-2.5-flash", "us-central1", adapter=False),
+    "legacy_non_gemini": Route("chat-bison", "us-central1", adapter=False),
+    "tuned_gemini_endpoint": Route(
+        "9876543210", "us-central1", adapter=False, overrides={"base_model": "vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-flash"}
+    ),
+}
+_ADAPTER_ROUTES: Final = tuple(name for name, route in _ROUTES.items() if route.adapter)
+
+
+def _openai_reply(model: str) -> dict[str, JsonValue]:
+    return {
+        "id": f"chatcmpl-{uuid.uuid4().hex}",
+        "object": "chat.completion",
+        "created": 1700000000,
+        "model": model,
+        "choices": [{"index": 0, "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": _REPLY_TEXT}, "finish_reason": "stop"}],
+        "usage": {
+            "prompt_tokens": _PROMPT_TOKENS,
+            "completion_tokens": _COMPLETION_TOKENS,
+            "total_tokens": _PROMPT_TOKENS + _COMPLETION_TOKENS,
+        },
+    }
+
+
+def _openai_frames(model: str, include_usage: bool) -> tuple[bytes, ...]:
+    base: Final = {
+        "id": f"chatcmpl-{uuid.uuid4().hex}",
+        "object": "chat.completion.chunk",
+        "created": 1700000000,
+        "model": model,
+    }
+
+    def frame(chunk: Mapping[str, JsonValue]) -> bytes:
+        return f"data: {json.dumps({**base, **chunk})}\n\n".encode()
+
+    usage: Final = (frame({"choices": [], "usage": _openai_reply(model)["usage"]}),) if include_usage else ()
+    return (
+        frame(
+            {"choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {"role": "assistant", "content": _REPLY_TEXT}, "finish_reason": None}]}
+        ),
+        frame({"choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {}, "finish_reason": "stop"}]}),
+        *usage,
+        b"data: [DONE]\n\n",
+    )
+
+
+def _asks_for_usage(body: Mapping[str, JsonValue]) -> bool:
+    options: Final = body.get("stream_options")
+    return isinstance(options, dict) and options.get("include_usage") is True
+
+
+def _native_reply() -> dict[str, JsonValue]:
+    return {
+        "candidates": [
+            {"content": {"parts": [{"text": _REPLY_TEXT}], "role": "model"}, "finishReason": "STOP", "index": 0}
+        ],
+        "usageMetadata": _USAGE,
+    }
+
+
+def _native_frames() -> tuple[bytes, ...]:
+    return (
+        b'data: {"candidates":[{"content":{"parts":[{"text":"'
+        + _REPLY_TEXT.encode()
+        + b'"}],"role":"model"},"index":0}]}\n\n',
+        b'data: {"candidates":[{"content":{"parts":[],"role":"model"},"finishReason":"STOP","index":0}],"usageMetadata":'
+        + json.dumps(_USAGE).encode()
+        + b"}\n\n",
+    )
+
+
+def _publisher_not_found(request: Request) -> Reply:
+    return Reply(
+        status=404,
+        body=json.dumps(
+            {
+                "error": {
+                    "code": 404,
+                    "message": f"Publisher Model {request.target} was not found",
+                    "status": "NOT_FOUND",
+                }
+            }
+        ).encode(),
+    )
+
+
+def _google_native_target(target: str) -> bool:
+    return any(
+        name in target for name in ("/models/gemini-2.5-flash:", "/models/chat-bison:", "/endpoints/9876543210:")
+    )
+
+
+def _vertex_peer(status: int = 200, error: str = "scripted vertex rejection") -> Callable[[Request], Reply]:
+    def respond(request: Request) -> Reply:
+        if status != 200:
+            return Reply(status=status, body=json.dumps({"error": {"message": error, "code": status}}).encode())
+        if request.target.endswith("/chat/completions"):
+            body: Final = _JSON_OBJECT.validate_json(request.body)
+            model: Final = str(body.get("model", ""))
+            if body.get("stream") is True:
+                return Reply(content_type="text/event-stream", chunks=_openai_frames(model, _asks_for_usage(body)))
+            return Reply(body=json.dumps(_openai_reply(model)).encode())
+        if request.target.endswith(":predict"):
+            return Reply(body=json.dumps({"predictions": _openai_reply("gemma-2-2b-it")}).encode())
+        if not _google_native_target(request.target):
+            return _publisher_not_found(request)
+        if ":streamGenerateContent" in request.target:
+            return Reply(content_type="text/event-stream", chunks=_native_frames())
+        if request.target.endswith(":countTokens"):
+            return Reply(body=json.dumps({"totalTokens": _NATIVE_COUNT}).encode())
+        return Reply(body=json.dumps(_native_reply()).encode())
+
+    return respond
+
+
+def _deployment(gateway: Gateway, scenario: Scenario, wire: Wire, route: Route, **extra: JsonValue) -> str:
+    return scenario.model(
+        model=f"vertex_ai/{route.model}",
+        api_base=f"{wire.url}{route.endpoint_path}",
+        api_key=None,
+        vertex_project=_PROJECT,
+        vertex_location=route.location,
+        vertex_credentials=service_account_json(_PROJECT, gateway.upstream_url.rstrip("/")),
+        **dict(route.overrides or {}),
+        **extra,
+    )
+
+
+def _contents(marker: str) -> list[JsonValue]:
+    return [{"role": "user", "parts": [{"text": f"route probe {marker}"}]}]
+
+
+def _generate(gateway: Gateway, model: str, key: str, body: Mapping[str, JsonValue]) -> httpx.Response:
+    return gateway.request("POST", f"/v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent", body, key=key)
+
+
+def _stream(gateway: Gateway, model: str, key: str, body: Mapping[str, JsonValue]) -> httpx.Response:
+    return gateway.client.post(
+        f"/v1beta/models/{model}:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse",
+        json=dict(body),
+        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"},
+    )
+
+
+def _frames(response: httpx.Response) -> list[dict[str, JsonValue]]:
+    parts: Final = [part for part in response.text.split("\n\n") if part.strip()]
+    assert all(part.startswith("data: ") for part in parts), response.text
+    return [_JSON_OBJECT.validate_json(part.removeprefix("data: ")) for part in parts]
+
+
+def _finish_reasons(frames: Sequence[Mapping[str, JsonValue]]) -> list[JsonValue]:
+    return [
+        object_value(candidate).get("finishReason")
+        for frame in frames
+        for candidate in (frame.get("candidates") or [])  # comprehension-ok: two-level frame walk
+        if isinstance(candidate, dict) and candidate.get("finishReason")
+    ]
+
+
+def _text(frames: Sequence[Mapping[str, JsonValue]]) -> str:
+    return "".join(
+        str(object_value(part).get("text", ""))
+        for frame in frames
+        for candidate in (frame.get("candidates") or [])  # comprehension-ok: three-level frame walk
+        for part in object_value(object_value(candidate).get("content") or {}).get("parts") or []
+    )
+
+
+def _spend_rows(key: str, count: int) -> list[dict[str, JsonValue]]:
+    digest: Final = sha256(key.encode()).hexdigest()
+    eventually(lambda: read_rows(_SPEND_SELECT, (digest,)), lambda values: len(values) >= count, seconds=70)
+    return held(lambda: read_rows(_SPEND_SELECT, (digest,)), lambda values: len(values) == count, holding=3)
+
+
+def _route_targets(wire: Wire) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
+    return [(request.method, request.target) for request in wire.drain()]
+
+
+def _expected_adapter_target(route: Route) -> str:
+    return route.endpoint_path if route.endpoint_path else "/chat/completions"
+
+
+def _cost_map_prices(gateway: Gateway, model: str) -> tuple[float, float]:
+    entries: Final = gateway.get("/model/info")["data"]
+    assert isinstance(entries, list)
+    info: Final = next(
+        object_value(object_value(entry)["model_info"])
+        for entry in entries
+        if object_value(entry)["model_name"] == model
+    )
+    prompt: Final = info.get("input_cost_per_token")
+    completion: Final = info.get("output_cost_per_token")
+    assert isinstance(prompt, float) and isinstance(completion, float) and prompt > 0 and completion > 0, info
+    return prompt, completion
+

+        }, rows

title: [Feature]: Expose OpenTelemetry trace IDs on LiteLLM Proxy responses

judge.reasoning: The issue asks for a specific header, `x-litellm-trace-id`, carrying the root trace ID as a 32-character lowercase W3C trace ID. Patch B implements exactly that: an ASGI middleware mounted inside the FastAPI instrumentor adds the header on the first `http.response.start` (covering JSON, streaming initial headers, and all exception-handler responses), stamps `litellm.call_id` on the server span from the response's `x-litellm-call-id`, preserves inbound `traceparent` (the server span already continues it), omits the header when the span is not recording or the gate is off, and handles the Starlette `ServerErrorMiddleware` 500 path by stashing the id on `request.state` and copying it in the unhandled-exception handler. Its unit tests exercise every scenario the issue enumerates (200, stream, 400/401/403/429/502/500, 422, traceparent round-trip, call_id on span, excluded route, no-op provider, gate off) and use the proxy's real exception handlers. Patch A instead emits a `traceresponse` header in `00-<trace>-<span>-<flags>` format and never adds `x-litellm-trace-id` at all. However well-engineered its propagator, upstream-relay linking, and CORS exposure are, it does not deliver the header the issue requests, so a client following the issue's user flow still cannot find the trace ID under the documented name. The independent tests confirm this: all ten trace-id tests fail on Patch A exactly as on base and pass on Patch B. Patch A also widens scope considerably (upstream traceresponse relaying, span links, CORS changes, a large integration test suite), which adds risk without addressing the ask. Patch B is the correct, scoped fix.

## Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate

## The Feature

Add `x-litellm-trace-id` to LiteLLM Proxy HTTP responses whenever the request has a recording OpenTelemetry server span. Its value should be the root trace ID as a 32-character lowercase W3C trace ID

The response already includes `x-litellm-call-id`, but a gateway user who receives that ID cannot reliably open the exact trace that handled the request. The proposed response header would make a client response, the request trace, and the existing call ID directly navigable across tracing and logging backends

For any response that has both values, the root server span should also carry the same `litellm.call_id` as `x-litellm-call-id`. This establishes an explicit relationship between the response, root span, and downstream LLM spans

Expected behavior:

1. Return the header on successful JSON responses and the initial headers of streaming responses
2. Return the header on validation, authentication, authorization, rate-limit, provider, and unhandled-error responses
3. Preserve incoming `traceparent` propagation and return the resulting request trace ID
4. Omit the header when OpenTelemetry is disabled or no recording request span exists
5. Keep `x-litellm-call-id` behavior unchanged

This is a LiteLLM Proxy / AI Gateway feature only. It does not change the Python SDK or WebSocket behavior

Related: #31864 covers request identity in JSON logs. This request covers the gateway HTTP response and its OpenTelemetry root span

## User Flow

Before this feature (today): a gateway developer investigating a failed model request reaches the response's call ID but cannot navigate directly to the trace that handled it

1. They send `POST https://gateway.example.com/v1/chat/completions` with their model and messages
2. The gateway returns `400 Bad Request` or a provider error with `x-litellm-call-id: 7ac48d62-40a1-44e6-8b50-19da641835a5`
3. They search the observability backend for that call ID and manually inspect matching LLM spans, logs, or request time ranges to identify the parent request trace
4. Their workaround is to correlate timestamps and child-span fields, which is slow and ambiguous when several retries or requests are in flight

After this feature (ideal user flow): the same developer can open the exact request trace from the gateway response

1. They send the same `POST https://gateway.example.com/v1/chat/completions` with the same model and messages
2. The gateway returns the same status and `x-litellm-call-id`, plus `x-litellm-trace-id: af353cab815b907430a117c9b97b4d0e`
3. They paste `af353cab815b907430a117c9b97b4d0e` into their observability backend and open the one server trace for that gateway request
4. They use the call ID visible on that trace to correlate request logs and downstream model spans without matching timestamps by hand

## How far you got

Config / setup the proxy ran with:

```yaml

general_settings:
  master_key: sk-local-trace-repro
litellm_settings:
  telemetry: false
```

Version or commit: `5417abd58672` on the current `main` branch

Environment variables: `LITELLM_OTEL_V2=true`, `OTEL_EXPORTER=console`, and `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=litellm-trace-header-repro`

Commands and their full output, up to the step that dead-ends:

```console
$ LITELLM_OTEL_V2=true OTEL_EXPORTER=console OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=litellm-trace-header-repro uv run litellm --config /private/tmp/litellm-trace-header-repro.yaml --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4000

HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request

x-litellm-call-id: 7ac48d62-40a1-44e6-8b50-19da641835a5

{"error":{"message":"/chat/completions: Invalid model name passed in model=missing-model. Call `/v1/models` to view available models for your key.","type":"invalid_request_error","param":null,"code":"400","provider_specific_fields":{"error":"/chat/completions: Invalid model name passed in model=missing-model. Call `/v1/models` to view available models for your key."}}}
```

The console exporter emitted this server span for the same request:

```console
{
    "name": "POST /v1/chat/completions",
    "context": {
        "trace_id": "0xaf353cab815b907430a117c9b97b4d0e",
        "span_id": "0x20cb45e2212a998e"
    },

```

What stopped me there: the live proxy created a server trace with ID `af353cab815b907430a117c9b97b4d0e` and returned a different call ID, but the HTTP response did not expose the trace ID. A client receiving the error therefore cannot navigate straight to the trace

## Which part of LiteLLM is this about?

Logging: callbacks, Langfuse, Datadog, OTel, Prometheus, alerting

+class _TraceIdResponseHeaderMiddleware:
+    """Expose the request's trace id as ``x-litellm-trace-id`` on HTTP responses.
+
+    Mounted directly inside the instrumentor's ``OpenTelemetryMiddleware`` so the
+    current span on entry is the request's server span, already parented on any
+    inbound ``traceparent``. The id is added to the first ``http.response.start``
+    message, which covers JSON bodies, error responses raised through the exception
+    middleware and the initial headers of streaming responses alike. The same
+    message's ``x-litellm-call-id`` is stamped on the server span as
+    ``litellm.call_id`` so the response, the root span and the LLM spans share it.
+    Requests with no recording span (excluded routes, provider not yet published)
+    get no header.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, app: "ASGIApp") -> None:
+        self.app = app
+
+    async def __call__(self, scope: "Scope", receive: "Receive", send: "Send") -> None:
+        if scope["type"] != "http":
+            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
+            return
+
+        from opentelemetry.trace import format_trace_id, get_current_span
+        from starlette.datastructures import MutableHeaders
+        from starlette.requests import Request
+
+        server_span: Final = get_current_span()
+        span_context: Final = server_span.get_span_context()
+        if not server_span.is_recording() or not span_context.is_valid:
+            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
+            return
+
+        trace_id: Final = format_trace_id(span_context.trace_id)
+        setattr(Request(scope).state, _TRACE_ID_STATE_KEY, trace_id)
+
+        async def send_with_trace_id(message: "Message") -> None:
+            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
+                headers: Final = MutableHeaders(scope=message)
+                # Assignment replaces any value already present (e.g. an upstream
+                # proxy's, copied through by a pass-through route).
+                headers[TRACE_ID_HEADER] = trace_id
+                call_id: Final = headers.get(_CALL_ID_HEADER)
+                if call_id and server_span.is_recording():
+                    server_span.set_attribute(LiteLLM.CALL_ID, call_id)
+            await send(message)
+
+        await self.app(scope, receive, send_with_trace_id)
+
+
+def stamp_trace_id_header(request: "Request", response: "Response") -> "Response":
+    """Add ``x-litellm-trace-id`` to a response sent outside the header middleware.

+    ``ServerErrorMiddleware``, outside every user middleware, so the handler copies
+    the trace id the middleware recorded on ``request.state`` itself.
+    """
+    trace_id: Final[object] = getattr(request.state, _TRACE_ID_STATE_KEY, None)
+    if isinstance(trace_id, str):

+from contextvars import ContextVar
+from typing import Final
+
+from opentelemetry import trace
+from opentelemetry.context import Context
+from opentelemetry.instrumentation.asgi import (  # pyright: ignore[reportMissingTypeStubs]  # the ASGI instrumentation ships no py.typed marker
+    asgi_getter,
+)
+from opentelemetry.instrumentation.propagators import ResponsePropagator
+from opentelemetry.propagators.textmap import CarrierT, Setter, default_setter
+from opentelemetry.trace import Span, format_span_id, format_trace_id
+from opentelemetry.trace.propagation.tracecontext import TraceContextTextMapPropagator
+
+from litellm.integrations.otel.model.semconv import LiteLLM
+
+_LITELLM_SERVER_SPAN: Final[ContextVar[Span | None]] = ContextVar(
+    "litellm_otel_traceresponse_server_span", default=None
+)
+
+
+def claim_server_span(span: Span) -> None:
+    _LITELLM_SERVER_SPAN.set(span)
+
+
+def _response_header(message: dict[str, object], name: str) -> str | None:  # mutable-ok: asgi_getter takes a dict
+    values: Final = asgi_getter.get(message, name)  # pyright: ignore[reportUnknownMemberType]  # the ASGI instrumentation ships no py.typed marker
+    return values[0] if values else None
+
+
+def _http_response_start(message: object) -> dict[str, object] | None:  # mutable-ok: the propagator writes into it
+    if isinstance(message, dict) and message.get("type") == "http.response.start":  # pyright: ignore[reportUnknownMemberType]  # an ASGI message is an untyped dict
+        return message  # pyright: ignore[reportUnknownVariableType]  # an ASGI message is an untyped dict
+    return None
+
+
+def _link_a_restarted_upstream_trace(span: Span, upstream_traceresponse: str) -> None:
+    upstream: Final = trace.get_current_span(
+        TraceContextTextMapPropagator().extract({"traceparent": upstream_traceresponse})
+    ).get_span_context()
+    if upstream.trace_id != span.get_span_context().trace_id:
+        span.add_link(upstream)
+
+
+class UpstreamFirstTraceResponsePropagator(ResponsePropagator):
+    def inject(
+        self,
+        carrier: CarrierT,
+        context: Context | None = None,
+        setter: Setter[CarrierT] = default_setter,
+    ) -> None:
+        start: Final = _http_response_start(carrier)
+        if start is None:
+            return
+        span: Final = trace.get_current_span(context)
+        if span is not _LITELLM_SERVER_SPAN.get():
+            return
+        call_id: Final = _response_header(start, "x-litellm-call-id")
+        if call_id:
+            span.set_attribute(LiteLLM.CALL_ID, call_id)
+        upstream_traceresponse: Final = _response_header(start, "traceresponse")
+        if upstream_traceresponse is not None:
+            _link_a_restarted_upstream_trace(span, upstream_traceresponse)
+            return
+        own: Final = span.get_span_context()
+        if not own.trace_flags.sampled:
+            return
+        sent: Final = start.get("headers")
+        if isinstance(sent, tuple):
+            start["headers"] = [*sent]
+        setter.set(
+            carrier,
+            "traceresponse",
+            f"00-{format_trace_id(own.trace_id)}-{format_span_id(own.span_id)}-{own.trace_flags:02x}",
+        )

+    return uuid.uuid4().hex
+
+
+def _span_id() -> str:
+    return uuid.uuid4().hex[:16]
